title.zh: 卷四百十九 列傳第一百七十八 宣繒 薛極 陳貴誼 曾從龍 鄭性之 李鳴復 鄒應龍 余天錫 許應龍 林略 徐榮叟 別之傑 劉伯正 金淵 李性傳 陳韡 崔福
title.en: Volume 419 Biographies 178: Xuan Zeng, Xue Ji, Chen Guiyi, Ceng Conglong, Zheng Xingzhi, Li Mingfu, Zou Yinglong, Yu Tianxi, Xu Yinglong, Lin Lüe, Xu Rongsou, Bie Zhijie, Liu Bozheng, Jin Yuan, Li Xingchuan, Chen Wei, Cui Fu
title.raw: 卷四百十九 列傳第一百七十八 宣繒 薛極 陳貴誼 曾從龍 鄭性之 李鳴復 鄒應龍 余天錫 許應龍 林略 徐榮叟 別之傑 劉伯正 金淵 李性傳 陳韡 崔福 Volume 419 Biographies 178: Xuan Zeng, Xue Ji, Chen Guiyi, Ceng Conglong, Zheng Xingzhi, Li Mingfu, Zou Yinglong, Yu Tianxi, Xu Yinglong, Lin Lüe, Xu Rongsou, Bie Zhijie, Liu Bozheng, Jin Yuan, Li Xingchuan, Chen Wei, Cui Fu

sentences.zh: 宣繒薛極陳貴誼曾從龍鄭性之李鳴復鄒應龍餘天錫許應龍林略徐榮叟別之傑劉伯正金淵李性傳陳韡

translations.literal: Xuan Zeng, Xue Ji, Chen Guiyi, Ceng Conglong, Zheng Xingzhi, Li Mingfu, Zou Yinglong, Yu Tianxi, Xu Yinglong, Lin Lüe, Xu Rongsou, Bie Zhijie, Liu Bozheng, Jin Yuan, Li Xingchuan, Chen Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Xuan Zeng, Xue Ji, Chen Guiyi, Ceng Conglong, Zheng Xingzhi, Li Mingfu, Zou Yinglong, Yu Tianxi, Xu Yinglong, Lin Lüe, Xu Rongsou, Bie Zhijie, Liu Bozheng, Jin Yuan, Li Xingchuan, and Chen Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈（崔福附）〉

translations.literal: (with Cui Fu appended)›
translations.idiomatic: (see also the biography of Cui Fu)

sentences.zh: 宣繒，慶元府人。

translations.literal: Xuan Zeng was a man of Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Zeng was a native of Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰三年，太學 兩優釋褐。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiatai, through double excellence at the Imperial University he was released from commoner status and entered office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiatai (1203), having earned top honors in both examinations at the Imperial University, he was released from commoner status and entered official service.

sentences.zh: 歷官以太學博士召試，為秘書省校書郎。

translations.literal: After successive posts he was summoned for examination as Doctor of the Imperial University and appointed Proofreader of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After serving in several posts, he was summoned for examination as Doctor of the Imperial University and appointed Proofreader of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 升著作佐郎兼權考功郎官、知吉州、福建提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Compiler, concurrently Acting Reviewing Affairs Officer, Prefect of Jizhou, and Fujian Judicial Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Compiler, and concurrently served as Acting Reviewing Affairs Officer, Prefect of Jizhou, and Fujian Judicial Intendant.

sentences.zh: 遷考功員外郎，又遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Reviewing Affairs, then again to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Reviewing Affairs and later to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時暫兼權侍立修注官、守起 居舍人，為起居郎兼權侍左侍郎，編《孝宗寶訓》。

translations.literal: At the time he temporarily also served concurrently as Acting Attendant Compiler, Acting Recorder of the Emperor's Movements, then as Recorder and concurrently Acting Vice Minister of the Left Secretariat, compiling the Precious Instructions of Emperor Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: For a time he also served concurrently as Acting Attendant Compiler and Acting Recorder of the Emperor's Movements, then as Recorder and concurrently Acting Vice Minister of the Left Secretariat, compiling the Precious Instructions of Emperor Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 試吏部侍郎，權兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was tried out as Vice Minister of Personnel and Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served on probation as Vice Minister of Personnel and Acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十四年，同知樞密院事兼參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiading he became Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Concurrent Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Jiading (1221), he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Concurrent Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 以資政殿學士奉祠。

translations.literal: He was made Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance and granted a sinecure temple appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance and granted a sinecure temple appointment.

sentences.zh: 端 平三年召赴闕，升大學士、提舉洞霄宮，以觀文殿大學士致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duanping he was summoned to court, promoted to Grand Academician and made Supervisor of the Dongxiao Palace, and retired as Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Duanping (1236) he was summoned to court, promoted to Grand Academician and made Supervisor of the Dongxiao Palace, and retired with the rank of Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈少師。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded the title Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously awarded the title Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 詔繒嘗預定策，以王堯臣故事贈太師，諡忠靖。

translations.literal: An edict stated that Zeng had once participated in fixing the succession; following the precedent of Wang Yaochén he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous title Loyal and Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: An edict noted that Zeng had once taken part in settling the succession; following the precedent of Wang Yaochén, he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Loyal and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 薛極，字會之，常州武進 人。

translations.literal: Xue Ji, style name Huizhi, was a man of Wujin in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ji, courtesy name Huizhi, was a native of Wujin in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 以父任調上元主簿。

translations.literal: Through his father's office he was appointed Recorder of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's official standing he was appointed Recorder of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 中詞科，為大理評事、通判溫州，知廣德軍。

translations.literal: He passed the Special Rhyme Examination, served as Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, Vice Prefect of Wenzhou, and Military Commissioner of Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Special Rhyme Examination and served as Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review, Vice Prefect of Wenzhou, and Military Commissioner of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 以參知政事樓鑰薦，遷大理正、刑部郎官，司封郎中、權右司郎中，遷右司郎中兼提領雜賣 場、寄樁庫，兼敕令所刪修官，中書門下省檢正諸房公事，兼刪修敕令官。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Vice Grand Councillor Lou Yue he was transferred to Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Officer of the Ministry of Justice, Director of the Bureau of Seals, and Acting Director of the Right Office; then Director of the Right Office concurrently in charge of the Miscellaneous Sales Market and the Commodity Reserve Depot, concurrently Compiler of Statutes at the Statute Revision Office, Inspector-General of the Various Bureaus of the Central Secretariat, and concurrently Compiler of Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Vice Grand Councillor Lou Yue, he rose to Director of the Court of Judicial Review, Officer of the Ministry of Justice, Director of the Bureau of Seals, and Acting Director of the Right Office; he was then made Director of the Right Office while also overseeing the Miscellaneous Sales Market and the Commodity Reserve Depot, serving as Compiler of Statutes at the Statute Revision Office, Inspector-General of the Various Bureaus of the Central Secretariat, and concurrently Compiler of Statutes.

sentences.zh: 拜司農卿兼權兵部侍郎，尋為真。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Revenue and Acting Vice Minister of War, and soon received the substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Revenue and Acting Vice Minister of War, and soon received the substantive appointment.

sentences.zh: 嘉定八年，疏奏：「願陛下深思顧諟之 難，益懷兢業之念。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiading he submitted a memorial: "I hope Your Majesty will deeply ponder the difficulty of reverent care, and further cherish thoughts of vigilant diligence.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiading (1215) he submitted a memorial: "I hope Your Majesty will deeply reflect on how hard it is to maintain reverent care, and cherish ever more the resolve to be vigilant in your duties.

sentences.zh: 勿謂帝德罔愆而怠於進修，勿以天災代有而應不以實。

translations.literal: Do not suppose that the imperial virtue is without fault and slacken in self-cultivation; do not, because calamities from Heaven occur in succession, respond without sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Do not suppose that your virtue is without flaw and grow slack in self-cultivation; do not, because Heaven sends calamity after calamity, answer them without genuine reform.

sentences.zh: 政綱雖舉，必求益其所未至；

translations.literal: Though the threads of government be raised up, you must seek to improve what has not yet been attained;
translations.idiomatic: Though the threads of government be raised up, you must still seek to improve what has not yet been attained;

sentences.zh: 德澤雖布，必思及其所未周。

translations.literal: though imperial favor be spread abroad, you must consider what has not yet been made complete.
translations.idiomatic: though your grace be spread abroad, you must still consider what has not yet been made complete.

sentences.zh: 誓以今日遇災警懼之心，永為 異時暇逸之戒。

translations.literal: Pledge that the heart of alarm and fear in meeting calamity today shall forever be a warning against leisure and ease in days to come.
translations.idiomatic: Pledge that the alarm and fear you feel today in the face of calamity shall forever warn you against ease and idleness in days to come.

sentences.zh: 將見天心昭格，沛然之澤響應於不崇朝之間。」

translations.literal: Then you will see Heaven's heart clearly moved, and a copious blessing respond within a single morning."
translations.idiomatic: Then you will see Heaven's heart clearly moved, and a copious blessing answer within a single morning."

sentences.zh: 遷權刑部尚書，尋試戶部尚書兼權吏部尚書，遂為真，時暫兼權戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Minister of Justice, then tried out as Minister of Revenue and Acting Minister of Personnel, soon received the substantive appointment, and for a time also temporarily served as Acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Acting Minister of Justice, then served on probation as Minister of Revenue and Acting Minister of Personnel, soon received the substantive appointment, and for a time also temporarily served as Acting Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十五年，特賜同進士出 身，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was specially granted the status of a jinshi by special decree and appointed Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Brightness and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was specially granted jinshi status by imperial decree and appointed Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Brightness and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，拜參知政事兼同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor and Concurrent Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoding (1228) he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor and Concurrent Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋知樞密院事兼參知政事，封毗陵郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Concurrent Vice Grand Councillor, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Piling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Concurrent Vice Grand Councillor, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Piling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 以觀文殿大學士知紹興府兼浙東安撫使。

translations.literal: As Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature he governed Shaoxing Prefecture and concurrently served as Pacification Commissioner of Eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature he governed Shaoxing Prefecture and concurrently served as Pacification Commissioner of Eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，加少保、和國公，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping he was given the additional titles Junior Guardian and Duke of the State of He, retired, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duanping (1234) he was given the additional titles Junior Guardian and Duke of the State of He, retired from office, and died.

sentences.zh: 陳貴誼，字正甫，福州福清人。

translations.literal: Chen Guiyi, style name Zhengfu, was a man of Fuqing in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guiyi, courtesy name Zhengfu, was a native of Fuqing in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 慶元五年進士，授瑞州觀察推官。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifth year of Qingyuan, he was appointed Investigating Aide of Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Qingyuan (1199), he was appointed Investigating Aide of Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁內外艱，服除，調安遠軍節度掌書記，辟差四川制置司書寫機宜文字。

translations.literal: He mourned the deaths of both parents; when the mourning period ended he was assigned as Secretary of the Anyuan Military Commission, and was specially recruited as Drafting Clerk for Military Affairs of the Sichuan Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning the deaths of both parents and completing the mourning period, he was assigned as Secretary of the Anyuan Military Commission and was specially recruited as Drafting Clerk for Military Affairs of the Sichuan Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 中博學宏詞科，授江南東路安撫司機宜文字。

translations.literal: He passed the Examination in Erudite Learning and Grand Eloquence and was appointed Clerk for Military Affairs of the Jiangnan East Route Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Examination in Erudite Learning and Grand Eloquence and was appointed Clerk for Military Affairs of the Jiangnan East Route Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 遷太社令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Altar of Earth and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Altar of Earth and Grain.

sentences.zh: 改武學諭、國子錄，遷太學博士。

translations.literal: He was changed to Instructor of the Military Academy and Registrar of the Directorate of Education, then transferred to Doctor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Instructor of the Military Academy and Registrar of the Directorate of Education, then promoted to Doctor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時議更楮幣法，貴誼轉對言：「人主令行禁止者，以同民之所好惡。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of changing the paper-currency law. In a court audience Guiyi said: "For a ruler's commands to be carried out and prohibitions enforced, he must share the people's likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was debating reform of the paper-currency law. In a court audience Guiyi said: "For a ruler's commands to be obeyed and his prohibitions enforced, he must share the people's likes and dislikes.

sentences.zh: 楮券之令，乃使奸惡獲逞，道路谘怨，非所以祈天永命、固結人心。」

translations.literal: The order on paper notes has only let the wicked prevail; the roads are full of complaint and resentment. This is not the way to pray to Heaven for enduring mandate and to bind the hearts of the people firmly."
translations.idiomatic: The order on paper notes has only let the wicked prevail, and the roads are full of complaint and resentment. This is not how to pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate or to bind the people's hearts firmly."

sentences.zh: 因援熙寧新法為辭。

translations.literal: He cited the New Policies of the Xining era in support of his argument.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the New Policies of the Xining era in support of his argument.

sentences.zh: 又 言：「明銳果敢之才，足以集事而失於剽輕；

translations.literal: He also said: "Men of keen insight and bold resolution are sufficient to gather affairs together yet fail through rash lightness;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Men of keen insight and bold resolution can get things done, yet they fail through rash impulsiveness;

sentences.zh: 老成寬博之士，足以厚俗而失於循理。

translations.literal: men of mature experience and broad learning are sufficient to enrich custom yet fail through mere adherence to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: men of mature experience and broad learning can enrich custom, yet they fail through mere adherence to precedent.

sentences.zh: 孰若舉之以眾，取之以公。」

translations.literal: How much better to raise them up through the multitude and select them through fairness."
translations.idiomatic: How much better to raise them up through public deliberation and select them through fairness."

sentences.zh: 主更幣之法者，乃摘新法等語激怒時相，且謂「貴 誼引類植黨」，人為危之。

translations.literal: Those who favored changing the currency law picked out his words about the New Policies and the like to enrage the chief minister, and added that "Guiyi gathers his kind and plants factions." People regarded him as in danger.
translations.idiomatic: Those who favored changing the currency law seized on his words about the New Policies and the like to enrage the chief minister, and moreover accused Guiyi of "gathering his kind and planting factions." Many thought him in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以兄貴謙兼禮部郎官，引嫌，遷將作監丞兼魏惠憲王府小學教授。

translations.literal: Because his elder brother Guiqian concurrently held the post of Officer of the Ministry of Rites, he cited conflict of interest and was transferred to Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and concurrently Instructor of the Primary School of the Princely Establishment of Prince Hui of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother Guiqian concurrently served as Officer of the Ministry of Rites, he cited conflict of interest and was transferred to Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and concurrently Instructor of the Primary School of the Princely Establishment of Prince Hui of Wei.

sentences.zh: 轉對，謂：「言路雖開，觸犯忌諱者指為好 名，切劘時政者指為玩令。

translations.literal: In a court audience he said: "Though the avenue of speech is open, those who touch on taboos are labeled seekers of fame, and those who cut sharply at current policy are labeled triflers with orders.
translations.idiomatic: In a court audience he said: "Though the avenue of speech is open, those who touch on taboos are labeled fame-seekers, and those who cut sharply at current policy are labeled triflers with the court's orders.

sentences.zh: 利害關於天下，是非公於人心。

translations.literal: What benefits or harms the realm concerns all under Heaven; right and wrong are public in the hearts of men.
translations.idiomatic: What benefits or harms the realm concerns all under Heaven; right and wrong are public in the hearts of men.

sentences.zh: 一人言之未已，或至累十數人言之，則又指為朋黨。

translations.literal: When one man has not finished speaking, or even when a dozen or more men speak, they are again labeled a faction.
translations.idiomatic: When one man has not finished speaking, or even when a dozen or more speak in turn, they are again labeled a faction.

sentences.zh: 是非易位，忠佞不分。」

translations.literal: Right and wrong change places; the loyal and the treacherous are not distinguished."
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong change places, and the loyal cannot be told from the treacherous."

sentences.zh: 史彌遠益不樂，遷秘書郎， 出知江陰軍，提舉江西常平。

translations.literal: Shi Miyuan was all the more displeased. Guiyi was transferred to Secretary of the Secretariat, sent out as Military Commissioner of Jiangyin, and made Supervisor of the Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan was all the more displeased. Guiyi was transferred to Secretary of the Secretariat, sent out as Military Commissioner of Jiangyin, and made Supervisor of the Jiangxi Ever-Normal Granaries.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在，未至，授禮部郎官。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the temporary capital; before he arrived he was appointed Officer of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the temporary capital; before he arrived he was appointed Officer of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 屬金人大擾淮、蜀，貴誼言：「人才所以立國，今旁蹊曲徑，幸門四辟。

translations.literal: When the Jin greatly disturbed Huai and Shu, Guiyi said: "Talent is what establishes a state. Today side paths and crooked byways open on every hand, and gates of favor stand wide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin greatly disturbed Huai and Shu, Guiyi said: "Talent is what establishes a state. Today side paths and crooked byways open on every hand, and gates of favor stand wide open.

sentences.zh: 言路所以通下 情，今弇阿循默，囊括不言。

translations.literal: The avenue of speech is what communicates the feelings of those below. Today there is flattery and compliant silence; everything is wrapped up and left unspoken.
translations.idiomatic: The avenue of speech is what communicates the feelings of those below. Today there is only flattery and compliant silence; everything is wrapped up and left unspoken.

sentences.zh: 民力已竭，而科斂之外，饋遺以謀進者未已。

translations.literal: The people's strength is already exhausted, yet beyond regular levies, gifts offered to seek advancement never cease.
translations.idiomatic: The people's strength is already exhausted, yet beyond regular levies, gifts offered to seek advancement never cease.

sentences.zh: 軍中恥言敗北，則陣亡者不恤；

translations.literal: In the army they are ashamed to speak of defeat, and so those who die in battle receive no care;
translations.idiomatic: In the army they are ashamed to speak of defeat, and so those who die in battle receive no care;

sentences.zh: 恥言棄潰，則逃竄者復招。」

translations.literal: ashamed to speak of rout and flight, they recruit back those who have fled."
translations.idiomatic: ashamed to speak of rout and flight, they recruit back those who have fled."

sentences.zh: 又言：「婉順巽從者，是災 疢也，非愛我也，宜屏之外之；

translations.literal: He also said: "Those who are meek and compliant are a plague upon you; they do not love you and should be kept at a distance;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Those who are meek and compliant are a plague upon you; they do not love you and should be kept at a distance;

sentences.zh: 矯拂救正者，是藥石也，愛我也，宜用之聽之。」

translations.literal: those who correct and admonish are medicine and stone; they love you and should be employed and heeded."
translations.idiomatic: those who correct and admonish you are medicine and stone; they love you and should be employed and heeded."

sentences.zh: 彌遠滋不樂，諷言者論罷，主管崇禧觀。

translations.literal: Miyuan was all the more displeased. Those who spoke against him had him dismissed from office, and he was made Supervisor of the Chongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan was all the more displeased. His critics had him dismissed from office, and he was made Supervisor of the Chongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 起知徽州，召授司封郎官兼翰林權直，兼玉牒所檢討。

translations.literal: He was recalled to govern Huizhou, then summoned and appointed Director of the Bureau of Seals, concurrently Acting Attendant of the Hanlin Academy, and concurrently Compiler at the Imperial Genealogy Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to govern Huizhou, then summoned and appointed Director of the Bureau of Seals, concurrently Acting Attendant of the Hanlin Academy, and concurrently Compiler at the Imperial Genealogy Office.

sentences.zh: 會有事明堂，首引包拯皇祐中乞因肆赦除聚斂掊克之敝，當察州縣府庫致羨之由。

translations.literal: When there was to be a ceremony at the Bright Hall, he first cited Bao Zheng's request in the Huangyou era to use the general amnesty to remove the abuses of exaction and squeezing, and that the causes by which prefectures, districts, and treasury offices produced surpluses should be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: When there was to be a ceremony at the Bright Hall, he first cited Bao Zheng's request in the Huangyou era to use the general amnesty to remove the abuses of exaction and squeezing, and urged that the causes by which prefectures, districts, and treasury offices produced surpluses should be investigated.

sentences.zh: 仿成周邦饗必及死王事者之子與漢置羽林孤兒，專取從軍死事之後，教以五兵。

translations.literal: Following the Zhou custom that at state banquets the sons of those who died in the king's service must be included, and the Han institution of the Orphan Sons of the Feathered Forest, he proposed to take exclusively the descendants of those who died in military service and teach them the five weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Zhou custom that at state banquets the sons of those who died in the king's service must be included, and the Han institution of the Orphan Sons of the Feathered Forest, he proposed to take exclusively the descendants of those who died in military service and teach them the five weapons.

sentences.zh: 理宗即位，以為宗正少卿兼侍講，兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, Guiyi was made Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court and Concurrent Lecturer, and concurrently Acting Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Lizong took the throne, Guiyi was made Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court and Concurrent Lecturer, and concurrently Acting Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 尋遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.

sentences.zh: 寶慶初，詔舉賢能才識之士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoqing an edict called for recommending men of worth, ability, and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoqing (1225) an edict called for recommending men of worth, ability, and discernment.

sentences.zh: 貴誼乃言曰：「世以容嘿滯固為賢，以苛刻生事為能，以褊狹趣辦 為才，以輕疏嘗試為識。

translations.literal: Guiyi then said: "The age takes taciturn dullness and obstinacy as worth, harshness and stirring up affairs as ability, narrowness and haste in getting things done as talent, and light carelessness and trial ventures as discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyi then said: "The age takes taciturn dullness and obstinacy as worth, harshness and stirring up affairs as ability, narrowness and haste in getting things done as talent, and light carelessness and trial ventures as discernment.

sentences.zh: 及茲初政，當求忠實正直、奉公愛民、知禮義廉恥而不越防範者，以充中外之選。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of this new reign you should seek men who are loyal, honest, upright, devoted to public duty and loving toward the people, who know ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame and do not overstep proper bounds, to fill selections within and without the court."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of this new reign you should seek men who are loyal, honest, upright, devoted to public duty and loving toward the people, who know ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame and do not overstep proper bounds, to fill selections within and without the court."

sentences.zh: 又言：「成王之初，元臣故老警以《無逸》者，欲其克 壽；

translations.literal: He also said: "At the beginning of King Cheng's reign, the great ministers and elders of old admonished him with the 'Against Idleness'—they wished him to achieve long life;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "At the beginning of King Cheng's reign, the great ministers and elders of old admonished him with the 'Against Idleness'—they wished him to achieve long life;

sentences.zh: 勉以敬德者，欲其永命；

translations.literal: those who exhorted him with reverent virtue wished him enduring mandate;
translations.idiomatic: those who exhorted him with reverent virtue wished him an enduring mandate;

sentences.zh: 期以豈弟者，欲其受命之長。

translations.literal: those who looked to him with kindness and forbearance wished his receiving of the mandate to be long.
translations.idiomatic: those who looked to him with kindness and forbearance wished his receiving of the mandate to be long.

sentences.zh: 則可謂愛君切而慮患深矣。」

translations.literal: This may be called loving the ruler earnestly and pondering calamity deeply."
translations.idiomatic: This may be called loving the ruler earnestly and pondering calamity deeply."

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人，升兼直學士院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafter of the Central Secretariat and promoted to concurrently serve as Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Drafter of the Central Secretariat and promoted to concurrently serve as Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 內侍濫受恩賞，輒封還詔書。

translations.literal: When eunuchs received favors and rewards improperly, he would seal and return the edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs received favors and rewards improperly, he would seal and return the edicts.

sentences.zh: 將郊，貴誼以：「民生實艱，吏員尚眾，征斂幾於奪取，公費掩為私藏。

translations.literal: When the suburban sacrifice was imminent, Guiyi submitted: "The people's livelihood is truly hard; official personnel are still numerous; levies are nearly outright seizure; public funds are hidden away as private stores.
translations.idiomatic: When the suburban sacrifice was imminent, Guiyi submitted: "The people's livelihood is truly hard; official personnel are still numerous; levies are nearly outright seizure; and public funds are hidden away as private stores.

sentences.zh: 宜大明黜陟，庶有以見帝於郊。」

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments should be made clearly manifest, so that there may be something by which to present the Emperor to Heaven at the suburban sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments should be made clearly manifest, so that there may be something worthy by which to present the Emperor to Heaven at the suburban sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，仍兼中書舍人、權刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, still concurrently Drafter of the Central Secretariat and Acting Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites, still concurrently Drafter of the Central Secretariat and Acting Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 升修玉牒官兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Compiler of the Imperial Genealogy and Concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Compiler of the Imperial Genealogy and Concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 為禮部尚書兼給事中、端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He became Minister of Rites, concurrently Supervising Secretary, Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Brightness, and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Rites, concurrently Supervising Secretary, Academician of the Hall of Illustrious Brightness, and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 紹定六年冬，上始親政，進參知政事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Shaoding the Emperor began to rule in person, and Guiyi was advanced to Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year of Shaoding (1233) the Emperor began to rule in person, and Guiyi was advanced to Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 上面諭之曰：「頃聞憂國之言，朕所不忘。」

translations.literal: The Emperor addressed him in person: "I have lately heard words of concern for the state, and I do not forget them."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor addressed him in person: "I have lately heard words of concern for the state, and I do not forget them."

sentences.zh: 兼同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was also made Concurrent Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Concurrent Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 出師汴、洛時，貴誼已移疾，猶上疏力爭。

translations.literal: When the army marched on Bian and Luo, Guiyi was already ill and had submitted his resignation, yet he still memorialized and argued strenuously.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched on Bian and Luo, Guiyi was already ill and had submitted his resignation, yet he still memorialized and argued strenuously against the campaign.

sentences.zh: 五上章乞歸，轉四官，加邑封，致仕。

translations.literal: Five times he submitted memorials asking to retire; he was transferred four ranks, given an enlarged fief, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Five times he submitted memorials asking to retire; he was transferred four ranks, given an enlarged fief, and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈少保、資政殿大學士。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Junior Guardian and Grand Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously awarded the titles Junior Guardian and Grand Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.

sentences.zh: 曾從龍，字君錫，左僕射公亮四世從孫。

translations.literal: Ceng Conglong, style name Junxi, was a fourth-generation collateral descendant of Left Vice Director Gongliang.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng Conglong, courtesy name Junxi, was a fourth-generation collateral descendant of Left Vice Director Gongliang.

sentences.zh: 初名一龍，慶元五年，擢進士第一，始賜今名。

translations.literal: His original name was Yilong. In the fifth year of Qingyuan he was placed first among jinshi and was then given his present name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yilong. In the fifth year of Qingyuan (1199) he placed first among jinshi and was then given his present name.

sentences.zh: 授簽書奉國軍節度判官廳公事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Signing Clerk for the Bureau of the Fengguo Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Signing Clerk for the Bureau of the Fengguo Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部員外郎、左司郎中、起居舍人兼太子右諭德。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of War, Director of the Left Office, and Recorder of the Emperor's Movements, concurrently Preceptor of the Right for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of War, Director of the Left Office, and Recorder of the Emperor's Movements, concurrently Preceptor of the Right for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 使金還，轉官。

translations.literal: On returning from an embassy to Jin he was transferred to another post.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from an embassy to Jin he was transferred to another post.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「州郡累月闕守，而以次官權攝者，彼惟其攝事也，自知非久，何暇盡心於民事？

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "When prefectures and districts go months without a prefect and the next official acts in his stead, knowing that he is only acting and will not remain long, how can he spare the mind to devote himself fully to the people's affairs?
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "When prefectures and districts go months without a prefect and the next official acts in his stead, knowing that he is only acting and will not remain long, how can he spare the mind to devote himself fully to the people's affairs?

sentences.zh: 獄訟淹延，政令玩弛，舉一郡之事付之胥吏。

translations.literal: Lawsuits drag on, government orders are treated lightly and grow slack, and the affairs of an entire commandery are entrusted to clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Lawsuits drag on, government orders are treated lightly and grow slack, and the affairs of an entire commandery are entrusted to clerks.

sentences.zh: 幸而除授一 人，民望其至如渴望飲，足未及境而復以他故罷去矣。

translations.literal: If by good fortune one man is appointed, the people look for his arrival as for thirsting after drink; yet before his foot has reached the border he is again removed for some other reason.
translations.idiomatic: If by good fortune one man is appointed, the people look for his arrival as for thirsting after drink; yet before his foot has reached the border he is again removed for some other reason.

sentences.zh: 且每易一守，供帳借請少不下萬緡。

translations.literal: Moreover, each time a prefect is changed, the costs of reception and borrowed funds are never less than ten thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, each time a prefect is changed, the costs of reception and borrowed funds are never less than ten thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 郡帑所入，歲有常數，而頻年將迎，所費不可勝計。

translations.literal: The income of the commandery treasury has a fixed annual amount, yet year after year the expenses of welcoming officials cannot be reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: The income of the commandery treasury has a fixed annual amount, yet year after year the expenses of welcoming officials cannot be reckoned.

sentences.zh: 然則輕於易置，公私 俱受其病。

translations.literal: Thus when prefects are changed lightly, both public and private alike suffer the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when prefects are changed lightly, both public and private alike suffer the harm.

sentences.zh: 欲望明詔二三大臣，郡守有闕，即時進擬。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will issue a clear edict to the chief ministers that when a prefecture lacks a prefect, a candidate shall at once be advanced for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will issue a clear edict to the chief ministers that when a prefecture lacks a prefect, a candidate shall at once be advanced for appointment.

sentences.zh: 其有求避憚行者，悉杜絕其請；

translations.literal: As for those who seek to avoid office out of fear, let all such requests be refused;
translations.idiomatic: As for those who seek to avoid office out of fear, let all such requests be refused;

sentences.zh: 其繳劾彈拄者，疾速行之。

translations.literal: As for those who submit memorials to impeach and obstruct [wrongdoing], let them be carried out with speed.
translations.idiomatic: Let memorials impeaching corrupt officials and blocking abuses be executed without delay.

sentences.zh: 蓋郡計寬則民力裕，利害常相關故也。」

translations.literal: For when the commandery's fiscal plan is broad, the people's strength is ample—benefit and harm are constantly mutually linked, hence this."
translations.idiomatic: When prefectural budgets are not squeezed to the bone, the people have room to recover, because public finance and popular welfare always rise and fall together.

sentences.zh: 又請已振 濟者免其後。

translations.literal: He also requested that those already given famine relief be exempted from [levies] thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that households already granted famine relief be exempt from further impositions.

sentences.zh: 開禧間丐外，知信州。

translations.literal: During the Kaixi era he begged for an outside posting and served as prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaixi period he sought a provincial appointment and became prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 戍卒行掠境內，從龍置於法，索得婦人衣，命梟於市。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers went about plundering within the borders; Conglong subjected them to the law, searched out women's garments, and ordered [the offender] displayed by decapitation in the market.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison troops looted the prefecture, Conglong prosecuted them under law, found women's clothing among the plunder, and had the culprit beheaded and his head exposed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 召權禮部侍郎兼中書舍人兼太子左諭德。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Acting Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, and concurrently Left Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Acting Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently Drafting Secretary and Left Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 繳還張鎡復官詞 頭，以鎡抑令侄女竭資財結姻蘇師旦之子故也。

translations.literal: He returned Zhang Zhen's draft edict for restoration to office, because Zhen had compelled his niece to exhaust her wealth to marry the son of Su Shidan.
translations.idiomatic: He vetoed the draft rescript restoring Zhang Zhen to office on the ground that Zhen had forced his niece to drain her property to marry Su Shidan's son.

sentences.zh: 尋兼太子諭德，兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰，兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as Preceptor to the Heir Apparent, concurrently Compiler of the National History, Associate Compiler of the Veritable Records Institute, and concurrently Director of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added the posts of Heir Apparent Preceptor, National History compiler, Veritable Records Institute associate compiler, and Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 為吏部侍郎，仍兼職兼太子右庶子，兼給事中，兼直學士 院，權刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He became Vice Minister of Personnel, still holding his concurrent posts, concurrently Right Subprefect of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Investigation Censor, concurrently Attendant of the Hanlin Academy, and Acting Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel while retaining his concurrent offices, adding Right Heir Apparent Subprefect, Investigation Censor, Hanlin attendant, and Acting Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 嘉定六年秋，陰雨，乞放繫囚。

translations.literal: In autumn of the sixth year of Jiading, with prolonged rain, he begged release of prisoners in custody.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Jiading 6, amid unending rains, he petitioned to release prisoners held in detention.

sentences.zh: 進對，言「修德政，蓄人材，飭邊備」。

translations.literal: Entering audience, he said, "Cultivate virtuous governance, store up talent, and rectify frontier defenses."
translations.idiomatic: At an imperial audience he urged, "Improve moral governance, cultivate talent, and strengthen border defenses."

sentences.zh: 帝善其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed his advice.

sentences.zh: 七年，知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he managed the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiading 7 he served as chief examiner for the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 疏奏：「國家以科目網羅天下之 英雋，義以觀其通經，賦以觀其博古，論以觀其識，策以觀其才。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "The state uses the examination subject to net the outstanding men of the realm; meaning-tests observe mastery of the Classics, fu observe breadth in antiquity, discourse essays observe insight, and policy questions observe talent.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The dynasty recruits the empire's finest through the examination system—Classicists to test mastery of the canon, rhapsodies to test breadth of antiquarian learning, discourse essays to test judgment, and policy questions to test practical ability.

sentences.zh: 異時謀王斷國，皆繇此其選。

translations.literal: In later days those who plotted as kings and decided the state all came from these selections.
translations.idiomatic: The statesmen who would one day counsel emperors and settle the fate of the realm were all chosen through these gates.

sentences.zh: 比來循習成風，文氣不振，學不務根祇，辭不尚體要，涉獵未精，議 論疏陋，綴緝雖繁，氣象萎苶。

translations.literal: Recently habit has become wind; literary spirit is not vigorous; learning does not aim at roots, phrasing does not esteem substance, skimming is not refined, discussion is crude and shallow; though compilation is abundant, the tone is wilted and feeble.
translations.idiomatic: Of late routine has hardened into fashion: writings lack vigor, students neglect fundamentals, diction ignores essentials, reading stays shallow, and argument grows slipshod. Papers multiply, yet their spirit sags.

sentences.zh: 願下臣此章，風厲中外，澄源正本，莫甚於斯。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would issue down this chapter of mine to exhort within and without, to clarify the source and correct the root—nothing is greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this memorial be circulated throughout court and country to reinvigorate standards at the source—no reform would matter more.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 進端明殿學士、簽書樞密院、太子賓客，改參知政事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Academician of the Duanming Hall, Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Guest of the Heir Apparent, and was changed to Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duanming Hall academician, Bureau of Military Affairs signing secretary, and Heir Apparent guest, then appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 疾胡榘憸壬，排沮正論，陳其罪。

translations.literal: He resented Hu Ju and sycophantic petty men, who repelled and obstructed upright discourse, and set forth their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced Hu Ju and his flatterers for suppressing honest debate and laid out their offenses.

sentences.zh: 榘嗾言者劾罷，以前職提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Ju incited remonstrators to impeach and dismiss him, and [Conglong] was made Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace with his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Ju instigated censors to impeach him out of office, after which he was sent to superintend the Dongxiao Palace at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 起知建寧府。

translations.literal: He was raised up to serve as prefect of Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，服除，為湖南安撫使。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended, he became Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death and the completion of mourning, he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 撫安峒獠，威惠並行，興學養士，湘人紀之石。

translations.literal: He pacified the cave Yao, combining awe and kindness; he raised schools and nurtured scholars, and the people of Xiang recorded him on stone.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the Yao hill peoples with a balance of firmness and grace, promoted schools and nurtured scholars, and the people of Hunan commemorated him on a stone inscription.

sentences.zh: 改知隆興府，復提舉洞霄宮，改萬壽觀兼侍讀，奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Longxing Prefecture, again made Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace, then changed to the Wanshou Observatory with concurrent Reader-in-Waiting, attending court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Longxing, again assigned to superintend the Dongxiao Palace, then moved to the Wanshou Observatory as Reader-in-Waiting with attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，授資政殿大學士、沿江制置使兼知建康府兼行宮留守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping he was granted Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall, Commissioner for Military Affairs along the River, concurrently Prefect of Jiankang Prefecture and concurrently Keeper of the Traveling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Duanping 1 he was appointed Zizheng Hall grand academician, Yangtze frontier commissioner, prefect of Jiankang, and keeper of the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 拜參知政事兼同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Grand Councilor and concurrently Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Grand Councilor and Associate Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時有三京之役，極論南兵輕進易退。

translations.literal: At the time there was the campaign for the Three Capitals; he argued forcefully that southern troops advance lightly and retreat easily.
translations.idiomatic: During the Three Capitals campaign he argued strenuously that southern armies were too quick to advance and too ready to retreat.

sentences.zh: 未幾言驗。

translations.literal: Before long his words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 進知樞密院事兼參 知政事，以樞密院使督視江淮、荊襄軍馬。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently Vice Grand Councilor, and as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs supervised the armies of Huai, Jiang, Jing, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of Military Affairs and Vice Grand Councilor, with charge of inspecting forces in the Huai-Jiang and Jing-Xiang regions.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「邊麵遼遠，聲援不接，請並建二閫。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "The frontier expanse is vast and remote, and mutual support does not connect; I request that two command headquarters be established together."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The frontier is vast and reinforcements cannot link up; I ask that two regional command headquarters be established at once.

sentences.zh: 詔許之，專畀江淮，以荊襄屬魏了翁。

translations.literal: An edict approved this; Huai and Jiang were exclusively entrusted [to Conglong], and Jing and Xiang were assigned to Wei Liaoweng.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved; Conglong was given sole charge of the Huai-Jiang front, while Jing-Xiang was assigned to Wei Liaoweng.

sentences.zh: 朝論邊用不給，詔從龍、了翁並領 督府。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that frontier expenses were insufficient, and an edict ordered Conglong and Liaoweng jointly to head the supervisory headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When court debate found border funds inadequate, an edict put both Conglong and Liaoweng in joint command of the supervisory headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及從龍卒，贈少師。

translations.literal: When Conglong died, he was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After Conglong's death he was posthumously honored as Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 弟用虎、天麟、治鳳，皆曆顯任。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Yonghu, Tianlin, and Zhifeng all passed through prominent appointments.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Yonghu, Tianlin, and Zhifeng all rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 鄭性之字信之，初名自誠，後改今名，福州人。

translations.literal: Zheng Xingzhi, courtesy name Xinzhi, was at first named Zicheng and later changed to his present name; he was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xingzhi (courtesy name Xinzhi), born Zicheng and later renamed, was from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，進士第一，歷官知贛州，改知隆興府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading he placed first among jinshi; in successive offices he was prefect of Ganzhou and was changed to prefect of Longxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He took first place in the Jiading 1 jinshi examinations, served as prefect of Ganzhou, and was later transferred to Longxing.

sentences.zh: 後以寶章閣待制提舉玉隆萬壽宮，進華文閣待制、提舉上清太平宮。

translations.literal: Later, as Awaiting Draftsman of the Baozhang Pavilion he superintended the Yulong Wanshou Palace; he was advanced to Awaiting Draftsman of the Huawen Pavilion and Superintendent of the Shangqing Taiping Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He later superintended the Yulong Wanshou Palace as Baozhang Pavilion awaiting draftsman, then advanced to Huawen Pavilion awaiting draftsman and superintendent of the Shangqing Taiping Palace.

sentences.zh: 進敷文閣待制、知建寧府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Awaiting Draftsman of the Fuwen Pavilion and Prefect of Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Fuwen Pavilion awaiting draftsman and prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 擢左諫議大夫，言：「台臣交章互詆，願陛下鑒古今天下安危之變，君子小人消長之機，公以處之，乃得其當。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Remonstrance Grandee and said: "Censors submit memorials back and forth mutual reviling; I hope Your Majesty will reflect on the changes in the realm's safety and peril from antiquity to today and on the waxing and waning of gentlemen and petty men, and with fairness dispose of them—then one obtains what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Left Remonstrance Grandee, he said: "Censors trade memorials denouncing one another. I urge Your Majesty to weigh how the realm's safety has shifted through history and how the influence of worthy men and petty men rises and falls, and judge between them with impartiality—that is the only fitting course.

sentences.zh: 況夫聽言之道，宜以事觀，若言果有關國體，有補治道，有益主德，則言之過激，夫亦何傷。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the way of listening to words one should view them by the matter: if the words truly concern the state's body, truly supplement the way of governance, and truly benefit the ruler's virtue, then even if the speech is excessive in vehemence, what harm is there?
translations.idiomatic: In hearing remonstrance, judge the substance: if a memorial truly bears on the state, improves governance, and strengthens the sovereign's virtue, what harm is there if its tone is sharp?

sentences.zh: 彼雖采名，我實有益。

translations.literal: Though they may seek reputation, I in fact receive benefit.
translations.idiomatic: They may court a reputation for bluntness, but the throne still gains.

sentences.zh: 惟虛心納善，若決江河，則激者自平矣。」

translations.literal: Only with an open mind receiving what is good, like deciding a river, will the vehement of themselves be calmed."
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty receives good counsel with an open heart, like a river finding its course, will heated words settle of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事，進同知樞密院事兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and was advanced to Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs with acting authority as Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Duanming Hall academician and Bureau of Military Affairs signing secretary, then promoted to associate commissioner with acting status as Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 尋拜參知政事兼同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor and concurrently Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Vice Grand Councilor and Associate Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋知樞密院事兼參知政事，加觀文殿學士，致仕。

translations.literal: Soon he became Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently Vice Grand Councilor; he was given the additional title of Academician of the Guanwen Hall and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Commissioner of Military Affairs and Vice Grand Councilor, was granted Guanwen Hall academician, and retired.

sentences.zh: 寶祐二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Baoyou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Baoyou 2.

sentences.zh: 鄒應龍，字景初。

translations.literal: Zou Yinglong, courtesy name Jingchu.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yinglong (courtesy name Jingchu).

sentences.zh: 慶元二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qingyuan 2.

sentences.zh: 歷官為起 居舍人，以直龍圖閣權知贛州，遷江西提點刑獄。

translations.literal: In successive offices he was Recorder of the Emperor's Movements; with the title of Direct Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall he acted as prefect of Ganzhou, and was transferred to Judicial Intendant of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Recorder of the Emperor's Movements, acted as prefect of Ganzhou as Direct Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and was transferred to Jiangxi Judicial Intendant.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書舍人兼太子右諭德，復兼太子左庶子、試戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat and concurrently Right Preceptor to the Heir Apparent; again he concurrently served as Left Subprefect of the Heir Apparent and Acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Drafting Secretary and Right Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, then also Left Heir Apparent Subprefect and Acting Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 使金還，為太子詹事兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: On returning from an embassy to Jin he became Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from an embassy to Jin he became Heir Apparent Mentor and Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中兼太子詹 事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Investigation Censor and concurrently Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Investigation Censor while retaining the post of Heir Apparent Mentor.

sentences.zh: 權禮部侍郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting Vice Minister of Rites and Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 權工部尚書兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: Acting Minister of Works and concurrently Compiler of the National History and Associate Compiler of the Veritable Records Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting Minister of Works while also compiling the National History and serving as associate compiler of the Veritable Records Institute.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 乞祠，以敷文閣學士提舉安慶府真原萬壽宮。

translations.literal: He begged for a temple appointment and, as Academician of the Fuwen Pavilion, superintended the Zhenyuan Wanshou Palace in Anqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a sinecure and was assigned to superintend the Zhenyuan Wanshou Palace in Anqing as Fuwen Pavilion academician.

sentences.zh: 以徽猷閣學士起知太平州，以臣僚論 罷。

translations.literal: As Academician of the Huixian Pavilion he was raised up to serve as prefect of Taiping Prefecture, and was dismissed on remonstrance by officials.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Huixian Pavilion academician to govern Taiping Prefecture, he was removed after officials impeached him.

sentences.zh: 以敷文閣學士提舉玉隆萬壽宮，拜禮部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: As Academician of the Fuwen Pavilion he superintended the Yulong Wanshou Palace and was appointed Minister of Rites with concurrent Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He superintended the Yulong Wanshou Palace as Fuwen Pavilion academician and was appointed Minister of Rites and Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaxi he was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaxi 1 he was appointed Duanming Hall academician and Bureau of Military Affairs signing secretary.

sentences.zh: 進資政殿學士、知慶元府兼沿海制置使，依舊職提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Academician of the Zizheng Hall, Prefect of Qingyuan Prefecture and concurrently Coastal Commissioner for Military Affairs, and in his former office continued to superintend the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Zizheng Hall grand academician, prefect of Qingyuan and coastal military commissioner, while retaining his superintendency of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 淳 祐四年卒，贈少保。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Chunyou and was posthumously granted Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chunyou 4 and was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 餘天錫，字純父，慶元府昌國人。

translations.literal: Yu Tianxi, courtesy name Chunfu, was a man of Changguo in Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tianxi (courtesy name Chunfu) was from Changguo in Qingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丞相史彌遠延為弟子師，性謹願，絕不預外事，彌遠器重之。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan invited him as tutor to his sons; by nature he was cautious and compliant, never involving himself in outside affairs, and Miyuan greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan engaged him as tutor to his sons. Tianxi was cautious and discreet, never meddling in outside affairs, and Miyuan held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 是時彌遠在相位久，皇子疆椓惡之，念欲有廢置。

translations.literal: At that time Miyuan had long been in the chief ministership; the imperial princes utterly detested him and thought of deposing him.
translations.idiomatic: By then Miyuan had held power for many years; princes in the palace loathed him and contemplated his removal.

sentences.zh: 會沂王宮無後，丞相欲借是陰立為後備。

translations.literal: It happened that the palace of the Prince of Yi had no heir; the chief councillor wished to use this opportunity secretly to establish a reserve successor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yi's household proved heirless, the chief councillor sought to use the occasion to groom a successor in secret.

sentences.zh: 天錫秋告歸試於鄉，彌遠曰：「今沂王無後，宗子賢厚者幸具以來。」

translations.literal: Tianxi took autumn leave to return home for the provincial examination; Miyuan said, "Now the Prince of Yi has no heir—if there are worthy and substantial clansmen, I hope you will bring them all."
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxi took leave to sit for the provincial examinations at home, Miyuan told him, "The Prince of Yi still has no heir—if you find any worthy and solid clansmen, bring them to me."

sentences.zh: 天錫絕江與越僧同舟，舟抵西門，天大雨，僧言門左有全保長者，可避雨，如其言過之。

translations.literal: Tianxi crossed the river in the same boat with a Yue monk; the boat reached the West Gate, and the sky poured with great rain; the monk said that to the left of the gate was the elder Quan Bao, where one could shelter from rain, and as he said they went there.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the river with a monk from Yue, Tianxi reached the West Gate in a downpour; the monk said that Quan Bao, an elder just inside the gate, would give them shelter, and they went to his house.

sentences.zh: 保長知為丞相館客，具雞黍甚肅。

translations.literal: Baochang knew him as a guest in the chief councillor's household and set out chicken and millet with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: Recognizing him as a client of the chief councillor, Baochang received him with a respectful meal of chicken and grain.

sentences.zh: 須臾有二子侍立，全曰：「此吾外孫 也。

translations.literal: Before long two sons stood in attendance; Quan said, "These are my grandsons by a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Presently two boys came forward to wait on them, and Quan said, "These are my grandsons.

sentences.zh: 日者嘗言二兒後極貴。」

translations.literal: The diviner once said these two boys would later be extremely noble."
translations.idiomatic: A fortune-teller had once said the boys would rise to supreme eminence.

sentences.zh: 問其姓，長曰趙與莒，次曰與芮。

translations.literal: He asked their surnames; the elder said Zhao Yuqi, the younger Yu Rui.
translations.idiomatic: When asked their names, the elder said Zhao Yuqi and the younger Zhao Yourui.

sentences.zh: 天錫憶彌遠所屬，其行亦良是，告於彌遠，命二子來。

translations.literal: Tianxi recalled what Miyuan had charged him with; their conduct was also truly good; he reported to Miyuan, who ordered the two sons to come.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi remembered Miyuan's commission, judged the boys promising, reported to him, and Miyuan summoned them.

sentences.zh: 保長大喜，鬻田治衣冠，心以為沂邸後可冀 也，集姻黨且詫其遇以行。

translations.literal: Baochang was greatly pleased, sold fields to prepare robes and caps, and in his heart thought that succession to the Yi princely residence might be hoped for; he gathered kinsmen and kin and boasted of their encounter as they set out.
translations.idiomatic: Overjoyed, Baochang sold land to outfit them properly, convinced they might be heirs to the Prince of Yi, and set out with kinsmen boasting of their good fortune.

sentences.zh: 天錫引見，彌遠善相，大奇之。

translations.literal: Tianxi introduced them; Miyuan was skilled at physiognomy and was greatly struck by them.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi presented them; Miyuan, skilled in reading faces, was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 計事泄不便，遽復使歸。

translations.literal: He reckoned that if the affair leaked it would be inconvenient, and abruptly had them sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure would be awkward, he quickly sent them home again.

sentences.zh: 保長大慚，其鄉人亦竊笑之。

translations.literal: Baochang was greatly ashamed, and the people of his village also secretly laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang was mortified, and his neighbors quietly mocked him.

sentences.zh: 逾年，彌遠忽謂天錫曰：「二子可復來乎？」

translations.literal: After a year Miyuan suddenly said to Tianxi, "Can the two sons come again?"
translations.idiomatic: A year later Miyuan abruptly asked Tianxi, "Can the two boys return?

sentences.zh: 保長謝不遣。

translations.literal: Baochang declined and would not send them.
translations.idiomatic: Baochang refused to send them.

sentences.zh: 彌遠密諭曰：「二子長最貴，宜撫於父家。」

translations.literal: Miyuan secretly instructed him: "Of the two sons the elder is most noble; he should be raised in the father's household."
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan secretly told him, "The elder boy is the more exalted; he should be brought up in his father's house.

sentences.zh: 遂載與歸。

translations.literal: He then had them loaded and brought back.
translations.idiomatic: They were then taken back with him.

sentences.zh: 天錫母朱為沐浴、教字，禮度益閑習。

translations.literal: Tianxi's mother Zhu bathed them and taught them characters; their ritual deportment grew ever more practiced and easy.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi's mother, Lady Zhu, bathed them and taught them to read; their manners grew steadily more polished.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召入嗣沂王，迄即帝位，是為理宗。

translations.literal: Before long [Yuqi] was summoned to succeed the Prince of Yi, and in the end ascended the imperial throne—this was Lizong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuqi was called in to succeed the Prince of Yi and eventually took the throne as Emperor Lizong.

sentences.zh: 天錫，嘉定十六年舉進士，歷監慈利縣稅，籍田令，超授起居舍人。

translations.literal: Tianxi, in the sixteenth year of Jiading, passed the jinshi examination; he passed through supervising the tax of Cili County, Registrar of the Imperial Fields, and was exceptionally appointed Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi passed the jinshi examinations in Jiading 16, served as supervisor of Cili county taxes and registrar of the imperial fields, and was exceptionally appointed Recorder of the Emperor's Movements.

sentences.zh: 遷權吏部侍郎兼玉牒所檢討官，兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Acting Vice Minister of Personnel and concurrently Reviser of the Imperial Genealogy Office, and concurrently Lecturer of the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Acting Vice Minister of Personnel and reviser of the Imperial Genealogy Office, and also lectured in the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎兼知臨安府、浙西安撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently Prefect of Lin'an Prefecture and Pacification Commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, prefect of Lin'an, and Pacification Commissioner of western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 試戶部 侍郎，權戶部尚書，皆兼知臨安府。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Vice Minister of Revenue and Acting Minister of Revenue, in each case concurrently Prefect of Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Acting and then Acting Minister of Revenue, in both cases also governing Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 升兼詳定敕令官，以寶文閣學士知婺州，仍舊職奉祠。

translations.literal: He was promoted to concurrently Detailed Reviser of Edicts and Statutes; as Academician of the Baowen Pavilion he was prefect of Wuzhou, still holding his former office in temple service.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to detailed reviser of edicts and statutes, appointed Baowen Pavilion academician and prefect of Wuzhou, while retaining his sinecure.

sentences.zh: 起知寧國府，進華文閣學士、知福州。

translations.literal: He was raised up to serve as prefect of Ningguo Prefecture, and was advanced to Academician of the Huawen Pavilion and Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to govern Ningguo, he was promoted to Huawen Pavilion academician and prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 召為吏部尚書兼給事 中兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of Personnel and concurrently Investigation Censor and concurrently Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Minister of Personnel, Investigation Censor, and Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 疏奏：「臣荷國恩，起家分閫，旋蒙趣覲，躐玷邇聯。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Your servant bears the state's grace; rising from a regional command, I was soon favored with a summons to audience and rashly stained the ranks nearest the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "I owe the dynasty a great debt: raised from a provincial command, I was soon summoned to court and undeservedly placed among Your Majesty's closest ministers.

sentences.zh: 時權禮部侍郎曹豳實在諫省，蓋嘗抗疏謂用臣大驟。

translations.literal: At the time Acting Vice Minister of Rites Cao Bin was in fact in the remonstrance office; he had once submitted a forceful memorial saying that employing your servant was too sudden.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cao Bin was serving as Acting Vice Minister of Rites in the remonstrance bureau and had once submitted a blunt memorial protesting my rapid promotion.

sentences.zh: 臣與豳父交最久，相知最深，今觀其所論，於 君父有陳善之敬，友朋有責善之道。

translations.literal: Your servant's friendship with Bin's father was longest, and our mutual understanding deepest; now viewing what he argues, toward ruler and father he has the reverence of presenting what is good, and toward friends he has the way of demanding what is good.
translations.idiomatic: I have long been closest to Bin's father and know him well. Reading his arguments now, I see the loyalty due a sovereign in offering honest counsel and the integrity due a friend in holding one to account.

sentences.zh: 而豳遂遷官，臣竟汙要路。

translations.literal: Yet Bin was then transferred in office, while your servant in the end stained a vital post.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Bin was promoted while I remained in a key post he had criticized.

sentences.zh: 豳以不得其言，累疏丐去。

translations.literal: Bin, because his words were not accepted, repeatedly submitted memorials begging to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Because his advice went unheeded, Bin repeatedly asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 夫亟用舊人而遂退二莊士，則將謂之何哉！

translations.literal: To urgently employ an old associate and thereby cause two upright gentlemen to withdraw—what will people say!
translations.idiomatic: If an old favorite is rushed into office while two upright men are pushed aside, what will the world say?

sentences.zh: 豳老成之望，直諒多益，置之 近班，可以正乃辟，可以儀有位。

translations.literal: Bin has the reputation of seasoned maturity; blunt honesty brings many benefits—place him in the near ranks and he can correct your assistants and can be a model for those in office.
translations.idiomatic: Bin enjoys the respect due a seasoned statesman; his frankness would benefit all. Keep him in the inner circle to correct your ministers and set an example for officeholders.

sentences.zh: 欲望委曲留行，使之釋然無疑，安於就職，則陛下既昭好賢之美，而微臣亦免妨賢之愧。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will tactfully detain him and keep him in office, causing him to release his doubts without suspicion and settle peacefully into his post—then Your Majesty will have displayed the beauty of loving worthies, and your humble servant will also escape the shame of obstructing worthies."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty graciously to keep him at his post, dispel his doubts, and let him serve in peace. You will show your love of talent, and I will be spared the shame of blocking it.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙二年，拜端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaxi he was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Co-Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaxi 2 he was appointed Duanming Hall academician and Co-Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋拜參知政事兼同知樞密院事，封奉化郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor and Concurrent Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fenghua Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became Vice Grand Councillor and associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with the title Duke of Fenghua.

sentences.zh: 授資政殿學士、知紹興府、浙東安撫使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance, Prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture, and Pacification Commissioner of Eastern Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Zizheng Hall academician, prefect of Shaoxing, and Eastern Zhe pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以觀文殿學士致仕。

translations.literal: He retired with the rank of Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He retired bearing the title Grand Academician of the Guanwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 朱氏亦封周、楚國夫人，壽過九十。

translations.literal: The Zhu clan was also enfeoffed as Ladies of Zhou and Chu, and lived past ninety.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhu was likewise ennobled as Lady of Zhou and Lady of Chu and lived beyond ninety years.

sentences.zh: 將以生日拜天錫為相，而天錫卒。

translations.literal: On his birthday the emperor was about to appoint Tianxi as chief councillor, but Tianxi died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to name Tianxi chief councillor on his birthday, but Tianxi died before it could happen.

sentences.zh: 贈少師，尋加太師，諡忠惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Junior Preceptor; soon afterward promoted to Grand Preceptor, with the posthumous epithet Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Preceptor, then Grand Preceptor, with the temple name Loyal and Kind (Zhonghui).

sentences.zh: 弟天任為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tianren was Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Tianren served as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 兄弟友愛，方貧時，率更衣以出，終歲同衾。

translations.literal: The brothers were affectionate; when poor they would take turns changing clothes before going out, and all year shared one quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply devoted to each other, in their poverty they shared what clothes they had and slept under one quilt throughout the year.

sentences.zh: 從子晦，歷官尚書，出帥全蜀，嘗置義壯，以贍宗族；

translations.literal: His nephew Hui rose to Minister; deployed as military commissioner over all Shu, he once established a righteous lodge to support the clan;
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Hui rose to minister and commanded all of Shu; he once founded a charity lodge to support their kinsmen;

sentences.zh: 然在蜀以違言論知閬州王惟忠死，士論少之。

translations.literal: Yet in Shu, because of a private grudge he caused Wang Weizhong, prefect of Langzhou, to die; scholar-official opinion looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Sichuan he had Prefect Wang Weizhong of Langzhou put to death over a personal grudge, and contemporaries thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 許應龍，字恭甫，福州閩縣人。

translations.literal: Xu Yinglong, courtesy name Gongfu, was a native of Min County in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yinglong (Gongfu) was from Min County, Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 五歲通經旨，坐客曰「小兒氣食牛」，應龍應聲「丈夫才吐鳳」為對，四坐嘉歎。

translations.literal: At five he grasped the gist of the classics; a guest said "The lad has the spirit to devour an ox," and Yinglong instantly replied "The gentleman's talent will spit the phoenix" as a counter-couplet; the whole assembly praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: At five he already understood the classics. When a guest remarked, "This boy has the mettle to devour an ox," Yinglong shot back, "A true man's talent will make the phoenix soar"—to the delight of all present.

sentences.zh: 入太學，嘉定元年舉進士。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University and in the first year of Jiading passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the Imperial University and passed the jinshi examinations in Jiading 1.

sentences.zh: 調汀州教授，差浙東 宣撫司掾，差戶部架閣。

translations.literal: Posted as professor at Tingzhou; detailed as clerk of the Eastern Zhe Pacification Commission; detailed as archivist of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as professor in Tingzhou, then served on the Eastern Zhe pacification staff and as an archivist in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷籍田令、太學博士。

translations.literal: Promoted to Registrar of the Imperial Fields and Doctor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to registrar of the imperial fields and doctor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時李全、時青輩歸附，應龍入對，有「{艸}蜂是懲，養虎遺患」之說，後皆如所言。

translations.literal: When Li Quan, Shi Qing, and their ilk submitted, Yinglong attended audience and said "Punish the stinging bee but leave the tiger to breed calamity"; later events all proved as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Quan, Shi Qing, and others defected to the Song, Yinglong warned the throne: "You punish the hornet but feed the tiger—and so breed future trouble." Events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 遷國子博士、國子丞、宗學 博士。

translations.literal: Promoted to Doctor of the National University, Vice Director of the National University, and Doctor of the Imperial Clan School.
translations.idiomatic: He became doctor of the National University, vice director of the National University, and lecturer at the imperial clan school.

sentences.zh: 招捕司遣統領官齊敏率師 由漳趨潮，截贛寇餘黨。

translations.literal: The Pacification Office dispatched Commander-in-chief Qi Min to lead troops from Zhang toward Chao to cut off the remnant bands of the Gan bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification office sent Commander Qi Min from Zhangzhou toward Chaozhou to mop up the survivors of the Ganzhou rebels.

sentences.zh: 應龍諭敏曰：「兵法攻瑕，今鍾寇將窮，陳寇猖獗，若先破鍾，則陳不戰禽矣。」

translations.literal: Yinglong instructed Min: "In warfare, attack the weak point; now the Zhong bandits are nearly exhausted while the Chen bandits run rampant—if you break Zhong first, Chen will be taken without a fight."
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong told Min: "Strike where the enemy is weak. The Zhong rebels are almost spent and the Chen rebels bold—crush Zhong first and Chen will fall without a fight."

sentences.zh: 敏惟命，於是諸寇皆平。

translations.literal: Min obeyed in all things, and thus all the bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Min followed his counsel, and every rebel band was subdued.

sentences.zh: 方未解嚴時，有行旅數人，隅總 搜其橐中金銀，指為賊黨。

translations.literal: While the emergency ban had not yet been lifted, several travelers had the gold and silver in their bags searched by subordinate commanders and were accused as bandit associates.
translations.idiomatic: Martial law had not yet ended when garrison officers searched several travelers' bags for gold and silver and accused them of colluding with bandits.

sentences.zh: 應龍辨其非盜，釋之，皆羅拜感泣。

translations.literal: Yinglong judged that they were not robbers, released them, and all bowed in gratitude, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong proved they were innocent merchants, set them free, and they prostrated themselves in tearful gratitude.

sentences.zh: 始，人疑應龍儒者不閑戎事，及見其區畫事宜，分別齊民，靜練雍容，莫不歎服。

translations.literal: At first people doubted that Yinglong the scholar was not versed in military affairs; when they saw him plan affairs, distinguish the common people clearly, and remain calm and dignified, all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At first skeptics thought a scholar like Yinglong unfit for war; when they saw how he organized the campaign, protected civilians, and bore himself with calm authority, they were won over.

sentences.zh: 僚屬請上功，應龍 曰：「守職捍城保民，何功之雲？」

translations.literal: His staff urged reporting merit; Yinglong said: "Guarding duty, defending the city, and protecting the people—where is merit to speak of?"
translations.idiomatic: When his staff urged him to claim credit, Yinglong said: "I only did my duty to defend the city and protect the people—what merit is there in that?"

sentences.zh: 距州六七十里曰山斜，峒獠所聚，丐耕土田不輸賦。

translations.literal: Sixty or seventy li from the prefecture was a place called Mount Xie, where cave Liao gathered; they begged to farm allotted fields but paid no tax.
