translations.idiomatic: Some sixty or seventy li from the prefectural seat lay Mount Xie, where cave-dwelling Liao had settled; they asked to farm allotments but refused to pay taxes.

sentences.zh: 禁兵與共，應龍平決之，其首感悅，率父老鳴缶擊筒，踴躍詣郡謝。

translations.literal: Garrison troops clashed with them; Yinglong judged and settled the matter; their chief was moved, and led the elders beating pots and striking tubes, leaping for joy as they came to the prefecture to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When Han garrison troops clashed with them, Yinglong adjudicated the dispute to everyone's satisfaction; the chieftain came to the city with his elders, drumming and dancing in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 去之 日，闔郡遮道攀送。

translations.literal: On the day he left, the whole prefecture blocked the road to detain and send him off.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed, the entire prefecture turned out to block the roads in farewell.

sentences.zh: 端平初，召為禮部郎官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping he was summoned as Bureau Secretary of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duanping era he was recalled as a secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 入對，帝謂應龍曰：「卿治潮有聲，與李宗勉治台齊名。」

translations.literal: Attending audience, the Emperor said to Yinglong: "In governing Chao you have a reputation, ranking with Li Zongmian's governance of Taiwan."
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor told Yinglong: "Your record at Chaozhou matches Li Zongmian's fame in Taiwan."

sentences.zh: 應龍頓首曰：「民無不可化，顧牧民者如何 耳。

translations.literal: Yinglong bowed his head and said: "The people can all be transformed—it depends only on how the shepherd of the people acts.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong kowtowed and replied: "No people are beyond reform; everything depends on how their governor behaves.

sentences.zh: 臣治州幸免曠瘝，皆陛下德化所暨，臣非曰能之。」

translations.literal: Your servant in governing the prefecture has fortunately avoided desolation and pestilence; it is all the reach of Your Majesty's transforming virtue—your servant does not claim ability."
translations.idiomatic: I have merely kept the prefecture from ruin—thanks to Your Majesty's benevolent rule, not to any skill of mine."

sentences.zh: 兼榮文恭王府教授，力辭，遷國子司業。

translations.literal: Concurrently professor of the Rongwen and Gong Prince's household, but he earnestly declined; transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered a concurrent post tutoring the Rongwen-Gong princes but declined firmly and was made vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 祭酒徐僑議學校差職，欲先譽望。

translations.literal: Director Xu Qiao proposed appointments at the schools based first on reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The director, Xu Qiao, wanted school posts filled by reputation first.

sentences.zh: 應龍以為不若差以資格，資格一 定，則僥幸之門杜而造請之風息。

translations.literal: Yinglong held that it was better to appoint by qualification; once qualification was fixed, the door of chance favor would be shut and the wind of lobbying would cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong argued for seniority instead: fixed rules would shut out favor-seeking and end the scramble for influence.

sentences.zh: 僑以為然。

translations.literal: Qiao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qiao accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 時有憑勢幹職者，力卻之。

translations.literal: When men relied on power to lobby for posts, he firmly refused them.
translations.idiomatic: He turned away anyone who used connections to demand appointments.

sentences.zh: 兼權直舍人院，遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Concurrently Acting Drafting Officer of the Secretariat, transferred to Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as acting draftsman and was promoted to chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 攝侍右侍郎兼學士院權直。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of the Right Secretariat and Concurrent Acting Academician and Acting Draftsman of the Hall of Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of the right secretariat and acting academician and draftsman.

sentences.zh: 是日，罷鄭清之、喬 行簡製，應龍所草也。

translations.literal: That day the dismissal edicts for Zheng Qingzhi and Qiao Jian were issued—Yinglong had drafted them.
translations.idiomatic: That same day edicts dismissed Zheng Qingzhi and Qiao Jianjian—edicts Yinglong himself had drafted.

sentences.zh: 翼日文德殿宣布畢，帝遣中使召應龍諭之曰：「草制甚善。」

translations.literal: The next day, when the announcement at the Wende Hall was finished, the Emperor sent a palace envoy to summon Yinglong and told him: "The draft was very good."
translations.idiomatic: The following day, after the edict was read in the Wende Hall, the emperor sent an envoy to tell Yinglong: "Excellent work on that draft."

sentences.zh: 應龍復謝曰：「臣聞昔人有言，進人若將加諸膝，退人若將墜諸淵。

translations.literal: Yinglong again thanked him and said: "Your servant has heard that ancients said: advancing a man is as though lifting him to your knee; demoting a man is as though letting him fall into an abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong thanked him again and said: "Your Majesty knows the old saying: to promote is to lift a man to one's knee; to dismiss is to let him fall into an abyss.

sentences.zh: 今二相乞罷 機政，與陛下體貌大臣之意，兩盡其美可也。」

translations.literal: Now the two chief councillors beg to leave the key offices; together with Your Majesty's intent to honor great ministers in deportment, both beauties may be fully achieved."
translations.idiomatic: The two councillors wish to resign; if Your Majesty treats them with the dignity owed senior ministers, both their honor and Your Majesty's will be served."

sentences.zh: 帝善之，就令草敕書戒諭諸閫。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved, and at once had him draft imperial letters admonishing the commandery-border officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and immediately ordered him to draft edicts of instruction to the frontier commanders.

sentences.zh: 權吏部侍郎兼侍講，兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Personnel and Concurrent Lecturer, and Concurrent Acting Academician of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was acting vice minister of personnel and lecturer, and also acting academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 試吏部侍郎，升侍讀，權兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Tried out as Vice Minister of Personnel, promoted to Lecturer, Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After a probationary term as vice minister of personnel, he became lecturer and acting minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時楮幣虧甚，行簡主行稱提之說，州縣希旨奉承，貧富猜懼。

translations.literal: At the time paper currency was severely depleted; Qiao Jian championed the policy of "lifting valuation"; prefectures and counties curried favor and complied, and rich and poor alike grew suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Paper money was badly depleted; Qiao Jianjian pushed "revaluation," and local officials slavishly complied until rich and poor alike were terrified.

sentences.zh: 應龍奏從民便、節用二說，行簡然之。

translations.literal: Yinglong memorialized two proposals—follow the people's convenience and economize expenditure—and Qiao Jian approved.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong urged easing the burden on the people and cutting state spending; Qiao Jianjian concurred.

sentences.zh: 兼吏部尚書，遷兵部兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Concurrently Minister of Personnel, transferred to Minister of War and Concurrent Imperial Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of personnel, then minister of war and imperial secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 三上章丐外，不允。

translations.literal: Three times submitted memorials begging for an outside post; not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked three times to leave the capital; each request was denied.

sentences.zh: 兼給事 中，兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Concurrently Supervisor of the Secretariat Chancellery, Concurrently Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as supervising censor and minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 請外，詔免兼中書，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He requested an outside post; an edict relieved him of the concurrent Secretariat post and appointed him Grand Academician of the Duanming Hall and Co-Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When he again sought a provincial post, the court removed his secretariat duties and named him Duanming academician and co-signing secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 累辭，會正言郭磊卿有論疏，以端明殿學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He repeatedly declined; when Remonstrator Guo Leiqing submitted a critical memorial, he was made Grand Academician of the Duanming Hall and Supervisor of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated refusals and a critical memorial from Remonstrator Guo Leiqing, he was sent to supervise the Dongxiao Palace as Duanming academician.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十有一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈資政殿學士、銀青 光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance and Silver-Gleaming Grandee of Glorious Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Zizheng Hall academician and Silver-Gleaming Grandee of Glorious Blessings.

sentences.zh: 應龍不躁不競，不激不隨，不妄薦士，而亦無傷人害物之事。

translations.literal: Yinglong was neither impetuous nor contentious, neither provocative nor compliant, did not recklessly recommend scholars, and also had no deeds of harming people or things.
translations.idiomatic: He was even-tempered and unassuming, neither hot-headed nor pliant, rarely pushed favorites, and never harmed others.

sentences.zh: 潮州之治，最可紀也。

translations.literal: His governance of Chaozhou is most worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: His tenure at Chaozhou remains the clearest measure of his worth.

sentences.zh: 林略，字孔英，溫州永嘉人。

translations.literal: Lin Lüe, courtesy name Kongying, was a man of Yongjia in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Lüe (Kongying) was from Yongjia, Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 慶元五年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qingyuan he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Qingyuan 5.

sentences.zh: 曆饒 州大寧監教授，辟幹辦四川茶馬司公事。

translations.literal: He passed through professor at the Daining Salt Supervisorate of Raozhou, and was invited as managing clerk of the Sichuan Tea and Horse Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He taught at Raozhou's Daining salt depot, then joined the Sichuan tea-and-horse commission as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 崔與之帥蜀，目之曰「此台閣之瑞也」，薦之。

translations.literal: Cui Yuzhi, as commander of Shu, fixed his gaze on him and said "This man is an auspice for the court," and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yuzhi commanded Sichuan, he called him "the court's good omen" and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 遷武學博士、國子監丞、太常寺丞。

translations.literal: Transferred to Doctor of the Martial Academy, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to doctor of the Martial Academy, vice director of the Directorate of Education, and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 奉祠，拜宗正少卿兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Received a sinecure appointment, and was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court and Concurrent Lecturer of the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After a temple sinecure he became vice director of the Imperial Clan Court and lecturer in the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 遷右 司諫，尋遷左司諫兼侍講，告於帝曰：「虛心以為從諫之本，從諫以為求治之本。」

translations.literal: Transferred to Right Bureau Remonstrator, soon transferred to Left Bureau Remonstrator and Concurrent Lecturer, reporting to the Emperor: "Taking an open mind as the root of accepting remonstrance, and accepting remonstrance as the root of seeking good government."
translations.idiomatic: He became right and then left remonstrator and lecturer, telling the emperor: "Open-mindedness is the foundation of heeding counsel; heeding counsel is the foundation of good government."

sentences.zh: 拜殿中侍御史，升侍御史，試右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Appointed Attendant Censor of the Palace, promoted to Attending Censor, tried out as Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace attendant censor, then attending censor, then acting right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙三年，以端明殿學士同簽書樞密 院事，以言罷，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaxi he was Grand Academician of the Duanming Hall and Co-Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs; dismissed because of a memorial, and made Supervisor of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaxi 3 he briefly served as Duanming academician and co-signing secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but a memorial drove him out to supervise the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 以資政殿學士致仕。

translations.literal: Retired with the rank of Grand Academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Zizheng Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 淳祐三年八月卒，特贈宣奉大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunyou, eighth month, he died; specially posthumously awarded Xuanfeng Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of Chunyou 3 and was posthumously given the rank Xuanfeng Grandee.

sentences.zh: 徐榮叟，字茂翁，煥章閣學士應龍之子。

translations.literal: Xu Rongsou, courtesy name Maoweng, was the son of the Huanchang Hall academician Yinglong.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Rongsou (Maoweng) was the son of Academician Xu Yinglong of the Huanchang Hall.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Jiading 7.

sentences.zh: 歷官通判臨安府，遷太學博士兼崇政殿說書，遷秘書郎，升著作佐郎兼侍左郎官。

translations.literal: He passed through posts as Transit Vice-Prefect of Lin'an Prefecture, Doctor of the Imperial University and Concurrent Lecturer of the Chongzheng Hall, Secretariat Gentleman, promoted to Assistant Compiler and Concurrent Left Secretariat Bureau Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was transit vice-prefect of Lin'an, doctor and lecturer at the Imperial University, secretariat gentleman, and then assistant compiler with a concurrent left-secretariat post.

sentences.zh: 出為江東提點刑獄，直秘閣、知婺州。

translations.literal: He went out as Judicial Intendant of Jiangdong, Direct Coordinator of the Secret Archive, and Prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital as Jiangdong judicial intendant, keeper of the secret archive, and prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷著作郎兼禮部郎官，以集英殿修撰知靜江府兼廣西經略安撫使。

translations.literal: Transferred to Compiler and Concurrent Bureau Secretary of the Ministry of Rites; as Compiler of the Hall of Assembled Excellence he was Prefect of Jingjiang Prefecture and Concurrent Guangxi Military Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became a compiler and ritual secretary, then Jingjiang prefect and Guangxi pacification commissioner with the rank Compiled at the Hall of Assembled Excellence.

sentences.zh: 召為行在司諫，復兼說書兼侍講。

translations.literal: Summoned as Remonstrator in the capital, again concurrently Lecturer and Concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as capital remonstrator, he again lectured at court.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙四年，拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaxi he was appointed Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaxi 4 he was appointed right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：「自楮幣不通，物價倍長，而民始怨；

translations.literal: Attending audience, he said: "From the time paper currency ceased to circulate, prices doubled and the people began to resent;
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said: "Ever since paper money stopped circulating, prices doubled and resentment began;

sentences.zh: 自米運多阻，粒食孔艱，而民益怨。

translations.literal: From the time grain transport met many obstacles, food became desperately scarce and the people resented all the more.
translations.idiomatic: ever since grain convoys were blocked, famine deepened and resentment grew worse;

sentences.zh: 此見之京師者然也。

translations.literal: This is so for those seen in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That is what we see in the capital.

sentences.zh: 外而郡邑，苛征橫斂，無所 不有，嚴刑峻罰，靡所不施。

translations.literal: Outside in commanderies and counties, harsh levies and extortionate collections exist nowhere that is not, severe punishments and stern penalties are applied nowhere that is not.
translations.idiomatic: In the provinces, crushing taxes and arbitrary fines are everywhere, and cruel punishments as well.

sentences.zh: 和糴則科抑以取贏，軍需則並緣而規利，逃亡強令代納，蠲放忍至重催。

translations.literal: In government purchase of grain they compel and press to seize profit; for military supplies they use pretexts to scheme for gain; those who flee are forcibly made to pay in their stead; where exemption is granted they still cruelly press for collection again.
translations.idiomatic: Official grain purchases are extortionate; military requisitions are milked for profit; refugees are forced to pay others' dues; tax relief is announced, then collections resume in earnest.

sentences.zh: 犯私販者不問多寡，概遭黥徒；

translations.literal: Those who violate private trade are not asked whether much or little—all uniformly suffer tattooing and penal servitude;
translations.idiomatic: Petty smugglers, guilty or not, are tattooed and sent to labor;

sentences.zh: 逋官課者不恤有無，動輒監繫。

translations.literal: Those who lag on official levies, regardless of whether they have means, are at once imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fall behind on official dues are jailed whether they can pay or not.

sentences.zh: 囹圄充斥，率是干連；

translations.literal: Prisons are packed full—all are cases of implication;
translations.idiomatic: Prisons overflow with men caught by guilt-by-association;

sentences.zh: 詞訟追呼，莫非枝蔓。

translations.literal: In lawsuits the pursued and summoned are all nothing but tangled branches.
translations.idiomatic: Every lawsuit spawns endless hangers-on.

sentences.zh: 如此則民安得而不怨？

translations.literal: In such circumstances how can the people not resent?
translations.idiomatic: How can people not boil with anger?

sentences.zh: 甚者富家巨室，武斷鄉閭，貴族豪宗，侵牟民庶。

translations.literal: What is worse, great rich households tyrannize the countryside, and noble powerful clans encroach on the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, wealthy magnates bully the countryside while great clans prey on commoners.

sentences.zh: 茹冤者不敢告，負抑者不得伸，怨氣薰 蒸，天示之應。

translations.literal: Those who swallowed injustice did not dare report; those who bore oppression could not plead—the resentment steamed up and Heaven showed a response.
translations.idiomatic: Victims dared not sue; the oppressed had no redress—until their wrath rose like steam and Heaven answered with omen.

sentences.zh: 此亢陽之所以為沴也。」

translations.literal: This is why the drought-heat has become a calamity."
translations.idiomatic: That is why drought and scorching heat punish the realm."

sentences.zh: 遷權禮部尚書兼權吏部尚書，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Transferred to Acting Minister of Rites and Concurrent Acting Minister of Personnel, appointed Grand Academician of the Duanming Hall and Co-Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was acting minister of rites and personnel, then Duanming academician and co-signing secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年乞歸田里，以資政殿大學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunyou he begged to return to his home village; he was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Great Governance and Supervisor of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou 2 he asked to retire home and was made Grand Academician of the Zida Hall, supervising the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉一官致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was advanced one rank and retired.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he was promoted one rank and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 別之傑，字宋才，郢州人。

translations.literal: Bie Zhijie, courtesy name Songcai, was a man of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bie Zhijie (Songcai) was from Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉定二年進士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiading he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Jiading 2.

sentences.zh: 歷官差充京西安撫司參議官，遷太府寺主簿，又遷將作監丞，差知澧州、知德安府。

translations.literal: He passed through posts as detailed participant on the Jingxi Pacification Commission staff, promoted to Chief Clerk of the Court of the Imperial Granary, again promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Works, detailed as Prefect of Lizhou, and Prefect of De'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the Jingxi pacification staff, rose to chief clerk of the imperial granary and vice director of imperial works, and governed Li and De'an prefectures.

sentences.zh: 親喪，起復，知德安府。

translations.literal: During parental mourning he was recalled to service, and served as Prefect of De'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Called back from mourning for his parents, he again governed De'an.

sentences.zh: 加直寶謨 閣、知江陵府、湖北安撫副使。

translations.literal: Promoted to Direct Coordinator of the Baomo Pavilion, Prefect of Jiangling Prefecture, and Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made keeper of the Baomo Pavilion, prefect of Jiangling, and deputy Hubei pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 進直煥章閣，言親年八十，乞祠歸養，庶幾君親之義兩全。

translations.literal: Promoted to Direct Coordinator of the Huanchang Pavilion; he said his parent was eighty and begged a sinecure to return and nurture them, that both the obligations to ruler and parent might be fully achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to keeper of the Huanchang Pavilion, he noted that his father was eighty and asked a sinecure so he could nurse him at home and honor both sovereign and parent.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 以京湖安撫制置使陳亥論罷，以前職主管崇禧觀。

translations.literal: Because the Jing-Hu Pacification Commissioner and Military Commissioner Chen Hai criticized him, he was dismissed; with his former post he supervised the Chongxi Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed after criticism from Jing-Hu commissioner Chen Hai, he retained his former rank while supervising the Chongxi Palace.

sentences.zh: 進直敷文閣、知 江陵府、湖北安撫使。

translations.literal: Promoted to Direct Coordinator of the Fuwen Pavilion, Prefect of Jiangling Prefecture, and Pacification Commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made keeper of the Fuwen Pavilion, prefect of Jiangling, and Hubei pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 起復，知真州，改知江寧府、湖北安撫副使，加兵部郎官，差充督視行府參謀官。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning, he was made prefect of Zhenzhou; changed to prefect of Jiangning Prefecture and Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Hubei, with the additional title of Vice Director in the Ministry of War, and assigned as planning staff officer for the supervisory field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he governed Zhenzhou, then Jiangning as deputy Hubei pacification commissioner and vice director of war, and was assigned as planning officer for the campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 遷軍器監，加直寶文閣、京西轉運判官兼提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Transferred to be Superintendent of the Armaments Directorate; given the additional posts of Honorary Keeper of the Baowen Pavilion, Western Capital Transport Commissioner, and Concurrent Judicial Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the armaments directorate, with honorary Baowen keeper, western capital transport commissioner, and judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 加秘閣 修撰、知江陵兼京湖制置副使。

translations.literal: Given the additional posts of Secretariat Archivist and Prefect of Jiangling, concurrently Deputy Military Commissioner for Jing and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made secretariat archivist, prefect of Jiangling, and deputy Jing-Hu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 進寶章閣待制、知太平州。

translations.literal: Advanced to Academic of the Baozhang Pavilion and Prefect of Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Baozhang academician and prefect of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 又進寶謨閣學士，依舊沿江制置使兼知建康府、江東安撫使。

translations.literal: Again advanced to Academician of the Baomo Pavilion; as before he was Military Commissioner along the Yangzi, concurrently Prefect of Jiankang Prefecture and Pacification Commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made Baomo academician while retaining his posts as Yangzi commissioner, Jiankang prefect, and Jiangdong pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 加兵部尚書兼淮西制置使，邊事聽便行之。

translations.literal: Given the additional posts of Minister of War and Concurrent Military Commissioner for Huai and Xi; frontier affairs were to be enacted at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Made minister of war and Huai-Xi commissioner, he was authorized to handle frontier matters as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 加端明殿學士。

translations.literal: Given the additional post of Academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Duanming academician.

sentences.zh: 淳祐二年，授同知樞密院事兼權參知政事，進資政殿學士、湖南安撫使兼知潭州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunyou he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Concurrent Acting Vice Grand Councilor; advanced to Academician of the Zicheng Hall, Pacification Commissioner of Hunan, and concurrently Prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou 2 he became vice commissioner of military affairs and acting vice grand councilor, then Zicheng academician, Hunan pacification commissioner, and prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 監察御史蔡次傳論罷。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Censor Cai Cichuan memorialized, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cai Cichuan impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he was made vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 乞歸田里，依前職知紹 興府，復以兩浙轉運判官翁甫論罷。

translations.literal: He begged to return to his home countryside; with his former post he was made prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture; again, through remonstrance by the Two Zhe Transport Commissioner Weng Fu, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire home, then governed Shaoxing under his former rank until transport commissioner Weng Fu of the Two Zhes impeached him again.

sentences.zh: 寶祐元年卒，特贈少師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyou he died; he was specially posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Baoyou 1 and was posthumously made junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 劉伯正，字直卿，饒州餘幹人。

translations.literal: Liu Bozheng, styled Zhijing, was a native of Yugan in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bozheng, courtesy name Zhijing, was from Yugan in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 父簡，為丞相趙汝愚客，嘗書慶曆四諫奏議授伯正，而伯 正以開禧元年舉進士。

translations.literal: His father Jian was a client of Chief Councilor Zhao Ruyu; he once copied and presented to Bozheng the memorials of the Four Remonstrators of Qingli; Bozheng passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Kaixi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian had served Chancellor Zhao Ruyu and once copied the Qingli remonstrators' memorials for his son; Bozheng passed the jinshi in Kaixi 1.

sentences.zh: 調太平主簿，通判棗陽軍，辟荊湖制置司機宜、兩浙轉運司主管公事。

translations.literal: Appointed registrar of Taiping; vice-prefect of Zaoyang Garrison; invited as confidential staff of the Jing-Hu Military Commission and Chief Clerk of the Two Zhe Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After registrar in Taiping and vice-prefect of Zaoyang, he was recruited to Jing-Hu staff and chief clerk on the Two Zhe transport commission.

sentences.zh: 曆軍器、將作、太府三監主簿，樞密院編修官，兵部郎官，監察御史。

translations.literal: He passed through registrar posts in the Armaments, Construction, and Treasury directorates; compiler in the Bureau of Military Affairs; Vice Director in the Ministry of War; and Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as registrar in the armaments, works, and treasury offices, then compiler at military affairs, vice director of war, and remonstrance censor.

sentences.zh: 有事於明堂，雷電忽至，執事者鮮不離次，伯正立殿下，紳笏儼然，聲色不動。

translations.literal: When there was a ceremony at the Hall of Enlightened Rule, thunder and lightning came suddenly; those presiding scarcely failed to leave their stations, but Bozheng stood below the hall, his girdle and tablet erect and dignified, neither voice nor expression changing.
translations.idiomatic: During a Hall of Enlightened Rule ceremony sudden thunder broke ranks among the officials, yet Bozheng stood below the throne belt and tablet straight, unshaken in face or voice.

sentences.zh: 帝遂以大任期之。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon greatly entrusted him with responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then entrusted him with weighty duties.

sentences.zh: 遷左司諫，疏言：「兵籍浸廣，糧餉益艱，請豫備軍 食。」

translations.literal: Transferred to Left Remonstrator; in a memorial he said: "The military registers gradually expand and provisions grow ever harder; I beg that army rations be prepared in advance."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to left remonstrator, he memorialized that armies were swelling, supplies tightening, and urged stockpiling rations.

sentences.zh: 又言銓選、財計、刑獄之積敝，「乞以願治之心而急董正治官之圖，以勤政之思而嚴察計吏之法」。

translations.literal: He also spoke of accumulated abuses in appointments, fiscal administration, and criminal justice: "I beg that with a mind desiring good governance you urgently oversee the plan to rectify officials, and with thoughts of diligent government strictly inspect the methods for revenue clerks."
translations.idiomatic: He also denounced abuses in appointments, finance, and justice, urging the emperor to reform officials in earnest and audit revenue clerks rigorously.

sentences.zh: 又言：「所憂非一，而急務之當慮者有三：曰申飭邊備， 區處流民，堤防奸盜。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The concerns are not single; urgent matters to consider are three: to tighten frontier defenses, settle wandering refugees, and guard against treacherous bandits."
translations.idiomatic: He identified three urgent tasks: reinforcing the frontier, resettling refugees, and suppressing banditry.

sentences.zh: 帝皆善其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised all his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved each proposal.

sentences.zh: 升右正言。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 以華文閣待制知廣州兼廣東經略安撫使。

translations.literal: As Academic of the Huawen Pavilion he was made prefect of Guangzhou and concurrently Guangdong Military Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As Huawen academician he governed Guangzhou and served as Guangdong military commissioner and pacifier.

sentences.zh: 召見，賜金帶鞍馬。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience; he was granted a gold belt and saddle horse.
translations.idiomatic: Called to court, he received a gold belt, saddle, and horse.

sentences.zh: 改轉運使，以寶章閣直學士知太平州。

translations.literal: Changed to transport commissioner; as Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion he was made prefect of Taiping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Made transport commissioner, he was then Baozhang academician and prefect of Taiping.

sentences.zh: 召為禮部侍郎 兼中書舍人，遷吏部侍郎兼侍講、同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: Summoned as Vice Minister of Rites and Concurrent Chief Drafting Secretary; transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel and Concurrent Lecturer, Co-compiler of the State History, and Co-compiler in the Veritable Records Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as vice minister of rites and drafting secretary, he became vice minister of personnel, court lecturer, state-history compiler, and veritable-records editor.

sentences.zh: 兼給事中，權刑部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Concurrently Supervising Secretary; Acting Minister of Punishments and Concurrent Reader.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as supervising secretary, acting minister of punishments, and reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou he was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall, Co-signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Concurrent Acting Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou 4 he became Duanming academician, co-signing secretary of military affairs, and acting vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 真拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Formally appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then confirmed as vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 以監察御史孫起予言罷，授資政殿學士、提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Through remonstrance by Remonstrance Censor Sun Qiyu he was dismissed; he was granted Academician of the Zicheng Hall and made Supervisor of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Sun Qiyu impeached him; he was given Zicheng academician rank and put in charge of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 監察御史蔡次傳言之，降一官，尋復舊官致仕。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Censor Cai Cichuan spoke against him; his office was lowered by one rank; shortly afterward he was restored to his former office and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Cai Cichuan spoke against him he was demoted one rank, then restored and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈正奉大夫，加少保。

translations.literal: He died; enfeoffed posthumously as Grandee of Proper Service; given the additional title of Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grandee of proper service and junior guardian.

sentences.zh: 時論謂伯正立朝，以靜重鎮浮，不求名譽，善藏其用云。

translations.literal: Opinion at the time said that Bozheng in court, with calm gravity reined in frivolity, did not seek reputation, and was adept at concealing his capabilities.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said that in office Bozheng steadied the court with quiet gravity, shunning fame while keeping his talents in reserve.

sentences.zh: 金淵，字淵叔，臨安府人。

translations.literal: Jin Yuan, styled Yuanshu, was a native of Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yuan, courtesy name Yuanshu, was from Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 嘉定七年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the seventh year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jiading 7.

sentences.zh: 歷官為太學博士，遷太府寺丞、秘書郎。

translations.literal: Through offices he served as Erudite of the National University; transferred to Assistant Director of the Treasury Directorate and Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from national university erudite to treasury assistant director and secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 升著作佐郎兼權司封郎官。

translations.literal: Promoted to Assistant Archivist and Concurrent Acting Vice Director in the Bureau of Enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to assistant archivist and acting director of enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞，拜右正言兼工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Transferred to Secretary of the Secretariat; appointed Right Remonstrator and Concurrent Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He became secretariat secretary and then right remonstrator with a concurrent vice ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 遷將作少監兼侍 右郎官，兼國子司業，兼國史編修、實錄檢討，兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Superintendent of Construction and Concurrent Attendant of the Right; concurrently Vice Chancellor of the National University; concurrently State History Compiler and Veritable Records Reviewer; concurrently Lecturer in the Hall for Venerating Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He next served as works vice superintendent and attendant of the right, university vice chancellor, state-history and veritable-records editor, and lecturer at the Hall for Venerating Governance.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，論曹豳、項寅孫。

translations.literal: Appointed Remonstrance Censor; he impeached Cao Bin and Xiang Yinsun.
translations.idiomatic: As remonstrance censor he impeached Cao Bin and Xiang Yinsun.

sentences.zh: 兼侍講，遷禮部侍郎，尋兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Concurrently Lecturer; transferred to Vice Minister of Rites; shortly afterward concurrently Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Also court lecturer, he became vice minister of rites and soon university chancellor.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，拜右諫議大夫， 改左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel; appointed Grandee of Remonstrance of the Right; changed to Grandee of Remonstrance of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice minister of personnel, then right and left remonstrance grandee in turn.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書兼給事中。

translations.literal: Transferred to Minister of Rites and Concurrent Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of rites and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，知貢舉，拜端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou he supervised the examination; appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Co-signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou 4 he oversaw the civil examinations and was made Duanming academician and co-signing secretary of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 侍御史劉漢弼論淵屍位妨賢，罷政予祠。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Liu Hanbi impeached Yuan for holding his post like a corpse while hindering the worthy; he was removed from government and granted a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censor Liu Hanbi accused Yuan of squatting in office and blocking talent; he left government for a sinecure post.

sentences.zh: 監察御史劉應起言，落職罷 祠。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Censor Liu Yingqi spoke; his office was struck and his sinecure revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Yingqi spoke against him, and he was stripped of rank and sinecure.

sentences.zh: 十一年，妻盛氏訴於朝，乞曲加貸宥，少敘官職。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, his wife Lady Sheng appealed at court, begging that he be graciously pardoned and given a modest restoration of office.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven his wife Lady Sheng petitioned the court to pardon him and restore him to a modest post.

sentences.zh: 詔止量移平江府居住。

translations.literal: An edict ordered only that he be relocated to reside in Pingjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The throne allowed him only to be reassigned to live in Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 李性傳，字成之，崇正寺主簿舜臣之子也。

translations.literal: Li Xingchuan, styled Chengzhi, was the son of Songchen, Registrar of the Chongzheng Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xingchuan, courtesy name Chengzhi, was the son of Chongzheng registrar Li Shunchen.

sentences.zh: 嘉定四年舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jiading 4.

sentences.zh: 曆幹辦 行在諸軍審計司。

translations.literal: He passed through as Staff Officer of the Capital Army Auditing Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer in the capital armies auditing office.

sentences.zh: 進對：「有崇尚道學之名，未遇其實。」

translations.literal: At audience he said: "There is the reputation of revering the Learning of the Way, yet its substance has not been encountered."
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said the court praised the Learning of the Way in name but had yet to meet its substance.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「實者何在？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Where lies the substance?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Where is that substance?"

sentences.zh: 性傳對曰：「在陛下格物致知，以為出治之本。」

translations.literal: Xingchuan replied: "In Your Majesty's investigating things and extending knowledge, as the root of emerging governance."
translations.idiomatic: Xingchuan answered that it lay in the emperor's investigating things and extending knowledge—the root of true governance.

sentences.zh: 遷武學博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Military Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was made erudite of the military academy.

sentences.zh: 尋為太常博士兼諸 王宮大小學教授。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Concurrent Professor in the great and small schools of the Princes' Palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became court of sacrifices erudite and professor in the princes' palace schools.

sentences.zh: 升太常寺丞兼權工部郎中，兼權都官郎官，遷起居舍人兼侍講。

translations.literal: Promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Sacrifices and Concurrent Acting Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; concurrently Acting Vice Director in the Bureau of Review; transferred to Diarist and Concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to sacrifices assistant director with acting posts in works and review, he became diarist and court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「東周以後，諸侯卿大夫皆以既葬而除服。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "After the Eastern Zhou, feudal lords, ministers, and grandees all doffed mourning once burial was complete.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that after the Eastern Zhou, lords and ministers ended mourning as soon as burial was finished.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢之際，尤為 淺促，孝文定為三十六日之制，則視孝惠以前已有加矣。

translations.literal: At the Qin and Han transition it was especially shallow and hurried; Emperor Xiaowen fixed a system of thirty-six days, which was already an increase compared with before Emperor Xiaohui.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin and Han mourning grew still shorter until Emperor Wen's thirty-six-day rule—already longer than before Emperor Hui.

sentences.zh: 東漢以後又損之為二十七日，謂之以日易月，則薄之至也。

translations.literal: After the Eastern Han it was again reduced to twenty-seven days, called substituting days for months—that is thinness to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han cut it to twenty-seven days, trading days for months—the thinnest conceivable observance.

sentences.zh: 千數百年，惟晉武帝、魏孝文為能復古之制，而 群臣沮格，未克盡行。

translations.literal: For a thousand-odd years, only Emperor Wu of Jin and Emperor Xiaowen of Wei were able to restore the ancient system, yet the ministers obstructed and blocked it and could not fully carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: For centuries only Emperors Wu of Jin and Xiaowen of Wei tried to restore ancient mourning, and even they were thwarted by their ministers.

sentences.zh: 惟孝宗通喪三年，近古所獨。

translations.literal: Only Emperor Xiaozong observed the full three-year mourning—a thing unique in recent antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Only Emperor Xiaozong kept the full three-year mourning, unmatched in recent times.

sentences.zh: 陛下繼之，至性克盡，前烈有光。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has continued it; utmost filial nature has been fully achieved, and the former exemplars shine.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has followed his example, fulfilling filial duty so fully that your forebears are honored.

sentences.zh: 乞以此疏付之史官，庶幾四海聞風，民德歸厚。」

translations.literal: I beg that this memorial be handed to the historiographers, that perhaps within the four seas customs may be heard and the people's virtue return to richness."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that this memorial enter the historical record, so all the realm might take notice and custom grow generous again."

sentences.zh: 遷起居郎，兼 國史編修、實錄檢討。

translations.literal: Transferred to Gentleman of the Household Who Attends; concurrently State History Compiler and Veritable Records Reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: He became attendant gentleman, state-history compiler, and veritable-records reviewer.

sentences.zh: 權刑部侍郎，進禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Punishments; advanced to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Acting vice minister of punishments, he rose to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 以臣僚言罷。

translations.literal: Through words of court officials he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow officials spoke against him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋以寶章閣待制知饒州，改知寧國府，再知饒州，復以言罷。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, as Academic of the Baozhang Pavilion he was made prefect of Raozhou; changed to prefect of Ningguo Prefecture; again prefect of Raozhou; again dismissed through remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Baozhang academician and prefect of Raozhou, then Ningguo, then Raozhou again—each time driven out by memorials.

sentences.zh: 召為兵部侍郎兼侍講，兼同修國史，兼 實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: Summoned as Vice Minister of War and Concurrent Lecturer; concurrently Co-compiler of the State History and Co-compiler in the Veritable Records Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as vice minister of war and lecturer, he also co-edited the state history and veritable records.

sentences.zh: 升兼侍讀，權兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Promoted to concurrent Reader; Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to reader-in-waiting, he was acting minister of war.

sentences.zh: 進讀《仁皇訓典》，乞讀《帝學》，從之。

translations.literal: He advanced to lecturing on the "Imperial Instructions of Emperor Renzong"; begged to lecture on the "Emperor's Learning"; the court assented.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured on Emperor Renzong's instructions, asked to teach the Emperor's Learning, and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 權吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 臣僚論舜臣立廟封爵事，落職，提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: Court officials impeached Shunchen's establishing a temple and enfeoffment; he was struck from office and made Supervisor of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When officials attacked his father's temple and enfeoffment, he was stripped of office and put in charge of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，權禮部尚書兼給事中，兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰，兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou, Acting Minister of Rites and Concurrent Supervising Secretary; concurrently Co-compiler of the State History and Co-compiler in the Veritable Records Institute; concurrently Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou 4 he was acting minister of rites and supervising secretary, co-editing histories and serving as reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall, Co-signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Concurrent Acting Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he became Duanming academician, co-signing secretary of military affairs, and acting vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 尋同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was vice commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，落職與郡。

translations.literal: Before long, his office was struck and he was given a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted and sent to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以資政殿大學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, as Grand Academician of the Zicheng Hall he supervised the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he was Zicheng grand academician supervising the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 寶祐二年，依舊職提舉萬壽觀兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoyou, with his former post he supervised the Wanshou Palace and concurrently served as Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoyou 2 he supervised the Wanshou Palace on his former rank and again served as reader.

sentences.zh: 以觀文殿學士致仕。

translations.literal: As Academician of the Guanwen Hall he retired.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Guanwen academician.

sentences.zh: 卒，特贈少保。

translations.literal: He died; specially posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made junior guardian.

sentences.zh: 十五年，淮西告捷，韡策金人必專向安豐而分兵綴諸郡，使卞整、張惠、李汝舟、範成進各以其兵屯廬州以待之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when Huai-Xi reported victory, Wei strategized that the Jurchens would surely aim at Anfeng exclusively while dividing troops to tie down the various prefectures; he had Bian Zheng, Zhang Hui, Li Ruzhou, and Fan Chengjin each camp their forces at Luzhou to await them.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen, after Huai-Xi victories, Chen Wei judged that the Jurchens would strike Anfeng while detachments pinned other prefectures, and stationed Bian Zheng, Zhang Hui, Li Ruzhou, and Fan Chengjin at Luzhou to meet them.

sentences.zh: 金將盧鼓捶新勝於潼關，乘銳急戰，當持久困 之，不過十日必遁，設伏邀擊，必可勝。

translations.literal: The Jin general Lu Guchui had newly won at Tong Pass and would press the fight with sharp momentum; one ought to wear him down over time—in no more than ten days he would surely flee; set ambushes to intercept and victory would certainly follow.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Lu Guchui was flush from Tong Pass and would fight recklessly; Wei urged wearing him down—within ten days he would flee—and then ambushing for a sure win.

sentences.zh: 又使時青、夏全候金人深入，以輕兵搗其巢穴，第一策也。

translations.literal: He also had Shi Qing and Xia Quan wait until the Jurchens penetrated deep, then strike their nest with light troops—the foremost stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Shi Qing and Xia Quan to wait until the Jurchens advanced deep, then raid their base with light troops—the best plan of all.

sentences.zh: 其後金人果犯安豐，韡如盱眙犒師。

translations.literal: Afterward the Jurchens indeed attacked Anfeng; Wei went to Xuyi to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens did attack Anfeng, Wei went to Xuyi to reward the army.

sentences.zh: 改淮東制置司幹辦公事。

translations.literal: Changed to Staff Officer of the Huaidong Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was made staff officer on the Huaidong military commission.

sentences.zh: 再 如盱眙見劉卓，調下整、張惠、範成進、夏全諸軍應援搗虛，皆行韡之策，遂有堂門之捷，俘其四駙馬者。

translations.literal: Again he went to Xuyi to see Liu Zhuo; he deployed Bian Zheng, Zhang Hui, Fan Chengjin, Xia Quan and the various armies to reinforce and strike the void—all following Wei's stratagem; thereupon came the victory at Tangmen, capturing their four coach horses.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Xuyi he met Liu Zhuo and ordered Bian, Zhang, Fan, and Xia to reinforce and raid behind enemy lines—all per Wei's plan—winning the battle at Tangmen and capturing four imperial coach horses.

sentences.zh: 遷將作監丞，又遷太府寺丞，差知真州、淮 東提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Transferred to Assistant Director of Construction; again transferred to Assistant Director of the Treasury Directorate; assigned as prefect of Zhenzhou and Judicial Intendant for Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to works and then treasury assistant director, he was assigned prefect of Zhenzhou and Huaidong judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 加直寶章閣，依舊提點刑獄兼知寶應州。

translations.literal: Given Honorary Keeper of the Baozhang Pavilion; as before Judicial Intendant, concurrently Prefect of Baoying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Made honorary Baozhang keeper, he kept his judicial post and governed Baoying.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正寺丞、權工部郎中，改倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: Transferred to Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and Acting Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; changed to Outer Vice Director in the Granary Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He became clan-court assistant director and acting works vice director, then outer director in the granary bureau.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：「臣所陳夏、周、漢、唐數君之事，如布德兆謀、任賢 使能、信賞必罰、區處藩鎮、不事姑息，規摹莫大於此。」

translations.literal: At audience he said: "What I have set forth of the several rulers of Xia, Zhou, Han, and Tang—such as spreading virtue and laying first plans, appointing the worthy and employing the able, trusting rewards and sure punishments, arranging and settling frontier garrisons, not practicing indulgence—no design is greater than this."
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said the lessons of Xia, Zhou, Han, and Tang—virtue, foresight, meritocracy, disciplined rewards and punishments, and firm control of far provinces without indulgence—formed the grand pattern of rule.

sentences.zh: 又言：「人主所以禦天下者，賞罰而已。」

translations.literal: He also said: "What a ruler uses to master all under Heaven is nothing but rewards and punishments."
translations.idiomatic: He added that a sovereign rules the realm through reward and punishment alone.

sentences.zh: 紹定二年冬，盜起閩中，帥王居安屬韡提舉四隅 保甲，韡有親喪，辭之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Shaoding, bandits rose in Minzhong; the commander Wang Ju'an charged Wei to supervise the four-corner baojia militias; Wei had a parent's mourning and declined.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoding 2 winter banditry erupted in Fujian; commander Wang Ju'an asked Wei to organize corner militias, but Wei declined because he was in mourning.

sentences.zh: 轉運使陳汶、提舉常平史彌忠告急於朝，謂非韡莫可平。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Chen Wen and Intendant for Ever-Normal Granaries Shi Miyou reported the emergency at court, saying that only Wei could pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Chen Wen and granary intendant Shi Miyou urged the court that only Wei could suppress them.

sentences.zh: 明年，以寶章閣直學士起復，知南劍州，提舉汀州、邵武軍兵甲公事，福建路兵馬 鈐轄，同共措置招捕盜賊兼福建路招捕使。

translations.literal: The next year, as Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion he was recalled from mourning; prefect of Nanjian Prefecture; charged with Fujian-route military affairs for Tingzhou and Shaowu Garrison; Military Controller-in-Chief of the Fujian Circuit; jointly arranging pursuit and capture of bandits, and concurrently Pursuit-and-Capture Commissioner for the Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The next year recalled from mourning as Baozhang academician, he governed Nanjian, oversaw arms in Ting and Shaowu, commanded Fujian-route forces, and led the circuit's bandit-suppression campaign.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Before long, given the additional post of Judicial Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 韡籍土民丁壯為一軍。

translations.literal: Wei registered the native people's adult males into one army.
translations.idiomatic: Wei enrolled local militia into a single army.

sentences.zh: 沙縣紫雲臺告急。

translations.literal: Ziyun Platform in Shaxian reported emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun Platform in Shaxian sent an urgent alarm.

sentences.zh: 沙縣破，賊由間道趨城，忠勇軍破之於高橋，賊乃趨邵武， 勢益熾。

translations.literal: Shaxian fell; the bandits by a bypath hastened toward the city; the Loyal-and-Brave Army defeated them at Gao Bridge; the bandits then hastened toward Shaowu, and their momentum grew fiercer still.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaxian fell the rebels took a mountain path toward the city, but the Loyal-and-Brave Army routed them at Gao Bridge; they then swerved toward Shaowu and their strength only swelled.

sentences.zh: 時有議當招不當捕者，韡言：「始者賊僅百計，招而不捕，養之至千，又養之至萬，今復養之，將至於無算。

translations.literal: At the time some argued one ought to summon them to surrender rather than pursue capture; Wei said: "At first the bandits numbered only in the hundreds; summoned and not captured, they were nurtured to a thousand, nurtured again to ten thousand—if we nurture them again now, they will grow beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged amnesty rather than pursuit; Wei replied that the rebels had grown from hundreds to thousands to tens of thousands through repeated indulgence, and to indulge them again would let their numbers swell beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 求淮西兵五千人可圖萬全。」

translations.literal: Request five thousand Huai-Xi troops and one may aim at complete security."
translations.idiomatic: He asked for five thousand Huai-Xi troops to make victory certain.

sentences.zh: 詔韡兼福建路招 捕使。

translations.literal: An edict made Wei concurrently Pursuit-and-Capture Commissioner of the Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The throne named him concurrent Fujian pursuit-and-capture commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊急攻汀州，淮西帥曾式中調精兵三千五百人由泉、漳間道入汀，擊賊於順昌勝之。

translations.literal: The bandits urgently attacked Tingzhou; Huai-Xi commander Zeng Shizhong mustered elite troops, three thousand five hundred men, who entered Ting by the bypaths of Quan and Zhang, defeated the bandits at Shunchang, and were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels pressed Tingzhou hard; Huai-Xi commander Zeng Shizhong sent 3,500 elite troops through Quan and Zhang bypaths into Ting and beat them at Shunchang.

sentences.zh: 六月，兵大合，加福建提點刑獄。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, troops assembled in great force; he was given the additional post of Fujian Judicial Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the armies united and he was also made Fujian judicial intendant.

sentences.zh: 七月，韡親提兵至沙縣、 順昌、將樂、清流、寧化督捕，所至克捷。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Wei personally led troops to Shaxian, Shunchang, Jiangle, Qingliu, and Ninghua to supervise pursuit, and wherever he arrived he gained victory.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wei led troops in person through Shaxian, Shunchang, Jiangle, Qingliu, and Ninghua, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 九月，分兵進討。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he divided troops to advance in punitive attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he split his forces for a general advance.

sentences.zh: 十月，進攻五賊營砦，平之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he advanced against the bandits' five camp forts and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month his men stormed five rebel forts and leveled them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，破潭瓦磜賊起之地，夷其巢穴。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he broke the place where the bandits had risen at Tanwazhen and razed their nests.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he smashed the rebels' cradle at Tanwazhen and destroyed their lairs.

sentences.zh: 十二月，誅汀州叛卒，諭降連城 七十有二砦，汀境皆平。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he executed the mutinous soldiers of Tingzhou, instructed surrender in seventy-two forts of Liancheng, and all within Ting territory was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he put down Tingzhou mutineers, accepted the surrender of seventy-two Liancheng forts, and pacified the whole prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，遣將破下瞿張原砦。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, he dispatched a general who broke the fort of Xiaqu Zhangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year four he sent a general to take the Xiaqu Zhangyuan fort.

sentences.zh: 二月，躬往邵武督捕餘寇，賊首晏彪迎降，韡以其力屈乃降，卒誅之。

translations.literal: In the second month, he went in person to Shaowu to supervise pursuit of the remnant bandits; the bandit chief Yan Biao came out to welcome and surrender; Wei, because he had surrendered only when his strength was exhausted, finally executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he went to Shaowu himself to mop up stragglers; rebel leader Yan Biao offered surrender, but Wei judged he had yielded only when beaten and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 進右文殿修撰，依舊提點刑獄、招捕 使兼知建寧府。

translations.literal: Promoted to Drafter of the Youwen Hall; as before Judicial Intendant and Pursuit-and-Capture Commissioner, concurrently Prefect of Jianning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Youwen drafter, he kept his judicial and bandit-suppression posts and governed Jianning.

sentences.zh: 衢州寇汪徐、來二破常山、開化，勢張甚。

translations.literal: Bandits of Quzhou, Wang Xu and Lai Er, broke Changshan and Kaihua; their momentum spread greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou rebels Wang Xu and Lai Er overran Changshan and Kaihua and grew formidable.

sentences.zh: 韡命淮將李大聲提兵七百，出賊不意，夜薄其砦，賊出迎戰，見算子旗，驚曰：「此陳招捕軍也！」

translations.literal: Wei ordered the Huai general Li Dasheng to lead seven hundred troops, strike where the bandits did not expect, and by night press close to their fort; the bandits came out to meet battle; seeing the banner with the counting-rods, they cried in alarm: "This is Pursuit-and-Capture Commissioner Chen's army!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Huai general Li Dasheng with seven hundred men to surprise the camp by night; when the rebels sallied forth and saw Chen's counting-rods banner they cried in terror, "It's Pursuit Commissioner Chen's troops!"

sentences.zh: 皆大 哭，急擊之，衢寇悉平。

translations.literal: All broke into loud weeping; he pressed the attack urgently, and the Quzhou bandits were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They wailed aloud; Li pressed the attack and the Quzhou rebels were crushed.

sentences.zh: 六年，進寶章閣待制、知隆興府。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, promoted to Recipient of the Baozhang Pavilion and Prefect of Longxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he became Baozhang recipient and prefect of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 贛寇陳三槍據松梓山砦，出沒江西、廣東，所至屠殘。

translations.literal: The bandit of Gan, Chen Sanqiang, held the fort of Songzi Mountain, appeared and vanished in Jiangxi and Guangdong, and wherever he went slaughtered and ravaged.
translations.idiomatic: Gan rebel Chen Sanqiang held Songzi Mountain, raided Jiangxi and Guangdong, and butchered wherever he struck.

sentences.zh: 韡遣官吏諭降，賊輒殺之。

translations.literal: Wei sent officials to instruct surrender; the bandits straightway killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent envoys to offer terms; the rebels killed them on sight.

sentences.zh: 乃謂盜賊 起於貪吏，劾其尤者二人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he said bandits and robbers arise from greedy officials, and impeached the two who were most extreme.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed corruption for the revolt and impeached the two worst officials.

sentences.zh: 又謂：「寇盜稽誅，以臣下欺誕、事權渙散所致，若決計蕩除，數月可畢。」

translations.literal: He also said: "That bandits and raiders tarry unpunished stems from subordinates' deception and dilution of command; if one resolves to sweep them away, within months it can be finished."
translations.idiomatic: He argued that delayed punishment came from deceit and divided authority, and that resolute action could finish the job in months.

sentences.zh: 十一月，詔節制江西、廣東、福建三路捕寇軍馬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, an edict placed him in command of the three circuits Jiangxi, Guangdong, and Fujian for pursuit of bandit troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was ordered to command Jiangxi, Guangdong, and Fujian forces against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 韡奏遣將 劉師直扼梅州、齊敏扼循州，自提淮西兵及親兵搗賊巢穴。

translations.literal: Wei memorialized dispatching the generals Liu Shizhi to choke off Meizhou and Qi Min to choke off Xunzhou; he himself would lead Huai-Xi troops and his personal guard to strike the bandits' nest.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed holding Meizhou with Liu Shizhi and Xunzhou with Qi Min while he led Huai-Xi and personal troops against the rebel base.

sentences.zh: 十二月，兼知贛州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, concurrently Prefect of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was also made prefect of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，賊跨三路數州六十砦，至是悉平。

translations.literal: At first the bandits spanned three circuits, several prefectures, and sixty forts; by this time all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had once held sixty forts across three circuits; now all were cleared.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「韡忠勤體國，計慮精審，身任討捕之責，江、閩、東廣，訖底寧輯。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Wei is loyal and diligent in embodying the state, his plans and reflections finely examined; he personally bore the responsibility of punitive pursuit; Jiang, Min, and eastern Guang—by the end all reached tranquil order."
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Wei's loyal service, shrewd planning, and personal leadership until Jiangxi, Fujian, and eastern Guangdong were pacified.

sentences.zh: 乃進權工部侍郎，仍知隆興兼江西安撫使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, still Prefect of Longxing and concurrently Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting vice minister of works, kept Longxing, and became Jiangxi pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為工部侍郎，改江東安撫使、知建康府，兼行宮留守。

translations.literal: Before long, made Vice Director of the Ministry of Works; changed to Jiangdong Pacification Commissioner and Prefect of Jiankang Prefecture, concurrently Keeper of the Traveling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became works vice minister, Jiangdong pacification commissioner, prefect of Jiankang, and keeper of the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 二年，入奏事，帝稱其平寇功，韡頓首言曰：「臣不佞，徒有孤忠，仗陛下威靈，苟逃曠敗耳，何功之 有。」

translations.literal: In the second year, he entered to memorialize affairs; the emperor praised his merit in pacifying bandits; Wei bowed his head and said: "Your servant is without talent, possessing only solitary loyalty; relying on Your Majesty's awesome numen, I barely escaped failure through dereliction—what merit is there?"
translations.idiomatic: In year two he reported at court; when the emperor praised his victories Wei kowtowed and said he was untalented, had only loyalty, and owed any success to the throne's grace.

sentences.zh: 遷權工部尚書，又權刑部尚書、沿江制置大使，依舊江東安撫使、知建康府。

translations.literal: Transferred to Acting Director of the Ministry of Works; again Acting Director of the Ministry of Punishments and Grand Commissioner for Pacification along the River; as before Jiangdong Pacification Commissioner and Prefect of Jiankang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became acting minister of works and punishments, riverine pacification grand commissioner, and kept his Jiangdong and Jiankang posts.

sentences.zh: 往來巡視鄂州江面，措置捍禦。

translations.literal: Back and forth he inspected the Yangtze face at Ezhou, arranging defense and resistance.
translations.idiomatic: He patrolled the Yangtze at Ezhou and organized the defenses.

sentences.zh: 三年，加寶謨閣學士。

translations.literal: In the third year, given Academician of the Baomo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he received the Baomo academician title.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔選猛將精兵，相 視緩急，據地利，遏要衝，以伐奸謀。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an edict ordered choosing fierce generals and elite troops, observing each other's urgency and ease, seizing terrain's advantage, blocking critical passes, to strike down treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the throne ordered picked generals and troops to watch conditions, hold favorable ground, and seal choke points against enemy plots.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙元年，進煥章閣學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaxi, advanced to Academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaxi 1 he became Huanzhang academician.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜刑部尚書，辭免。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, invested as Director of the Ministry of Punishments; he declined and was excused.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was offered minister of punishments but declined.

sentences.zh: 加徽猷閣學士、知潭州、荊湖南路安撫使。

translations.literal: Given Academician of the Huiyou Pavilion, Prefect of Tanzhou, and Pacification Commissioner of Jinghu South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became Huiyou academician, prefect of Tanzhou, and Jinghu South pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 淳祐四年，召 為兵部尚書，遷禮部尚書兼侍讀，兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunyou, summoned as Director of the Ministry of War; transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites, concurrently Court Reader, concurrently Co-compiler of the National History and Co-drafter in the Veritable Records Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunyou 4 he was summoned as war minister, then made rites minister, court reader, and co-historian of the state annals.

sentences.zh: 拜端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事兼參知政事。

translations.literal: Invested as Academician of the Duanming Hall, Co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Concurrent Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He became Duanming academician, co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and vice grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 尋拜參知政事兼同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Soon invested as Vice Grand Councillor, concurrently Co-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice grand councillor and co-director of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年，知樞密院事、湖 南安撫大使兼知潭州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Grand Pacification Commissioner of Hunan, concurrently Prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he directed the Bureau of Military Affairs, served as Hunan grand pacification commissioner, and governed Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，以觀文殿學士、福建安撫大使知福州，五上章辭，以舊職提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, as Academician of the Guanwen Hall and Grand Pacification Commissioner of Fujian he was Prefect of Fuzhou; five times he submitted memorials declining; with his former post he was made Director of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he was named Guanwen academician, Fujian grand commissioner, and Fuzhou prefect, but declined five times and retired to oversee Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，召赴闕，落致仕，充醴泉觀使兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiqing, summoned to the capital; his retirement was lifted; made Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey, concurrently Court Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiqing 1 he was recalled, his retirement revoked, and made Liquan commissioner and court reader.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，授 福建安撫大使兼知福州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingding, given the post of Grand Pacification Commissioner of Fujian, concurrently Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingding 1 he was again appointed Fujian grand commissioner and Fuzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 久之，提舉佑神觀，力請致仕。

translations.literal: After a long while, made Director of the Youshen Abbey; he urgently requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he oversaw Youshen Abbey and pressed hard to retire.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年八十有三。

translations.literal: The next year he died, age eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year at eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈少師，諡忠肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Junior Preceptor; posthumous title Loyal-and-Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior preceptor with the temple name Loyal-and-Solemn.

sentences.zh: 崔福者，故群盜，嘗為官軍所捕，會夜大雪，方與嬰兒同榻，兒寒啼不止，福不得寐，覺捕者至，因以故衣擁兒口，遂逸去。

translations.literal: Cui Fu was formerly of the mass bandits; once he was captured by government troops; it happened to snow heavily at night; he was just on the same couch with an infant; the child cried from cold without cease; Fu could not sleep; he sensed the captors had arrived; therefore with old clothes he smothered the child's mouth and thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Fu had been a bandit. Once when troops seized him on a snowy night, he was sharing a bed with a baby whose ceaseless crying kept him awake. Hearing his pursuers near, he muffled the infant with a garment and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 因隸軍籍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he entered the military registers.
translations.idiomatic: He then enlisted.

sentences.zh: 初從趙葵，收李全有功，名重江、淮，又累從韡捕賊，積功至刺史、大將軍。

translations.literal: At first he followed Zhao Kui; in receiving Li Quan he had merit; his name weighed heavy on the Yangtze and Huai; again he repeatedly followed Wei in pursuing bandits, accumulating merit until Inspector and Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Zhao Kui, won fame on the Huai for defeating Li Quan, then repeatedly fought bandits under Wei, rising to inspector and grand general.

sentences.zh: 後從韡留隆興。

translations.literal: Later he followed Wei and remained at Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He later stayed at Longxing with Wei.

sentences.zh: 既而韡移金陵，而福猶在隆興。

translations.literal: Before long Wei moved to Jinling, but Fu remained at Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei moved to Jinling, Fu stayed behind in Longxing.

sentences.zh: 屬通判與郡僚燕滕王閣，福恚其不見招，道遇民訴冤者，福攜其人直至飲所，責以郡官不理民事，麾諸卒盡碎飲 具，官吏皆惴恐竄去，莫敢嬰其鋒。

translations.literal: It happened that the vice-prefect and prefectural colleagues feasted at the Prince of Teng Pavilion; Fu resented that he was not summoned; on the road he met a commoner pleading injustice; Fu took the man straight to the drinking-place, reproached them that prefectural officials did not attend to the people's affairs, waved the various soldiers to smash all the drinking vessels entirely; officials and clerks all cowered in fear and fled away; none dared brush his edge.
translations.idiomatic: When the vice-prefect and staff banqueted at the Prince of Teng Pavilion without inviting him, Fu met a petitioner on the road, dragged the man into the feast, accused the officials of ignoring justice, and had his men smash all the tableware while officials fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 韡知之，遂檄建康，署為鈐轄。

translations.literal: Wei learned of it; thereupon he issued a dispatch to Jiankang and appointed him Controller-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Wei transferred him to Jiankang as controller-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 福又奪統製官王明鞍馬，及迫逐總領所監酒官親屬。

translations.literal: Fu again seized the campaign-commander Wang Ming's saddle horse, and also drove off the relatives of the wine-monopoly supervisor under the Chief Fiscal Office.
translations.idiomatic: Fu also seized campaign commander Wang Ming's horse and harassed the wine-tax inspector's family.

sentences.zh: 韡戒諭之，不聽。

translations.literal: Wei admonished and instructed him; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei warned him, but Fu paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 會淮兵有警，步帥王鑒出師，鑒請福行，韡因厚遣之。

translations.literal: It happened that Huai troops had an alarm; Infantry Commander Wang Jian went out with the army; Jian requested Fu to march; Wei therefore sent him off with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai troops came under threat, infantry commander Wang Jian took the field and asked for Fu; Wei sent him off with rich provisions.

sentences.zh: 福不樂為鑒用，遇敵不擊，托以葬女擅歸，亦不聞於制置司。

translations.literal: Fu did not delight in being used by Jian; encountering the enemy he did not strike; using burial of his daughter as pretext he returned on his own authority, nor did he report to the Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to serve Wang Jian, Fu refused to fight, left without leave to bury his daughter, and never informed headquarters.

sentences.zh: 鑒怒，遂白其前後過惡，請必正其慢令之罪。

translations.literal: Jian was angry; thereupon he reported his former and latter excesses and crimes, requesting that his crime of contempt for orders must be rectified.
translations.idiomatic: Jian furiously reported Fu's misconduct and demanded punishment for disobedience.

sentences.zh: 會韡亦厭忌之，遂坐以軍法，然後聲其罪於朝，且自劾專殺之罪。

translations.literal: It happened that Wei also loathed and feared him; thereupon he was punished by military law; only then did he proclaim his crimes at court, and moreover impeached himself for the crime of unauthorized killing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, who also resented him, executed Fu by military law, then reported the crimes to court while confessing summary execution.

sentences.zh: 下詔獎諭，免其罪。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to reward and instruct him; his crime was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised him by edict and pardoned the offense.

sentences.zh: 福勇悍善戰，頗著威聲；

translations.literal: Fu was brave, fierce, and skilled in battle; he quite established a reputation for awe.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was ferocious in battle and enjoyed wide renown;

sentences.zh: 其死也，軍中惜之。

translations.literal: At his death, within the army they regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: and the army mourned his death.

sentences.zh: 時論以為良將難得，而韡以私忿殺之。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time held that good generals are hard to obtain, yet Wei killed him from private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said a rare general had been lost to Wei's private spite.

sentences.zh: 然福跋扈之跡已不可掩，殺身之禍，亦有以自取之也。

translations.literal: Yet Fu's overbearing conduct could no longer be covered; the calamity of losing his life—he also had means by which to bring it on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fu's arrogance was undeniable, and he had partly brought his fate upon himself.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋自嘉定以來，居相位者賢否不同，故執政者各以其氣類而用之，因其所就而後世得以考其人焉。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: From the Jiaqing reign onward in Song, those who occupied the chief ministry differed in worth and unworth; therefore those who held power each employed men of their own temperamental kind; according to what they achieved, later ages may examine the men.
translations.idiomatic: The historians note that since Jiaqing, chief ministers differed in quality, and each faction appointed its own kind—so posterity can judge them by their deeds.

sentences.zh: 宣繒、薛極者，史彌遠之腹心也。

translations.literal: Xuan Zeng and Xue Ji were Shi Miyuan's belly-heart men.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Zeng and Xue Ji were Shi Miyuan's intimates.

sentences.zh: 陳貴誼、曾從龍、鄭性 之、李性傳、劉伯正，皆無所附麗。

translations.literal: Chen Guiyi, Ceng Conglong, Zheng Xingzhi, Li Xingchuan, and Liu Bozheng—all had nothing to which they attached and relied.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Guiyi, Ceng Conglong, Zheng Xingzhi, Li Xingchuan, and Liu Bozheng stood beholden to no faction.

sentences.zh: 李鳴復、金淵者，史嵩之之羽翼也。

translations.literal: Li Mingfu and Jin Yuan were Shi Songzhi's wing-and-feather men.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mingfu and Jin Yuan were Shi Songzhi's protégés.

sentences.zh: 鄒應龍無所考見，許應龍治郡見稱循良，林略所謂虛心從諫者，有益於人主矣。

translations.literal: For Zou Yinglong nothing can be examined and seen; Xu Yinglong in governing his prefecture was praised as orderly and good; of Lin Lüe it is said he was one who with empty mind followed remonstrance—beneficial to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: On Zou Yinglong little can be said; Xu Yinglong governed well; Lin Lüe, who heeded counsel, served his sovereign well.

sentences.zh: 徐榮叟父子 兄弟皆為名臣，陳韡將帥才也，優於別之傑多矣。

translations.literal: Xu Rongsou—father, sons, and brothers—all were famed ministers; Chen Wei had the talent of a general; he surpassed Bie Zhijie by far.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu Rongsou clan produced eminent ministers; Chen Wei was a born commander, far outshining Bie Zhijie.
